# Sophaxis: the policies and pages in full

Each part below is the Markdown from which the page at its address is built, word for word.

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html

# Terms of Use

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [利用規約（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

The laws, licences and terms that this page cites are quoted at the end of each section that cites them.
Japanese statutes are quoted in full, as the e-Gov law API gives them. The other texts are quoted word for word from their official sources, as fetched on 2026-11-11, and are not translated.
A citation whose source could not be fetched is named there as not quoted, with the reason.

## Who these terms apply to

These terms apply to everyone who reads Sophaxis or submits to it.
Authors agree to them in the submission form, in their version of the day.
Reading Sophaxis is not taken as agreement to anything; for readers, these terms describe how Sophaxis works, and the law decides what each side owes.
The other policies are part of these terms.
How content is moderated is set out in the Moderation Policy and the Takedown Policy, and every automatic step that takes part in it is listed on the page [What runs by itself](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/automation.html).

## What Sophaxis provides

Sophaxis lists preprints in philosophy, mathematics, logic, the philosophy of mathematics and the philosophy of science.
It gives each listed work a record page, a search, a feed and, where the repository allows, a copy of the PDF.
It does this free of charge.

## The authors bear full responsibility

The authors bear full responsibility for their work and for its listing on Sophaxis.
This covers:

- the content of the work, including every claim, proof, citation, calculation and figure;
- the right to share the version under its licence, and the permission of any publisher;
- material from others in the work, and any infringement of copyright or other rights;
- personal data of third parties in the work;
- the statement on generative models, and any use that it leaves out;
- the truth of everything the submitter confirms in the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html).

Moderation does not move any of this to the operator.
A listing says only that a submission passed the checks in the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html).
If a third party makes a claim against Sophaxis or its operator because something the submitter confirmed at submission is untrue, the authors are responsible for it, as the law provides.
Authors agree that the record page (its title, authors, abstract and PDF copy) may be taken offline while a removal request is reviewed under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html), and that OAI-PMH then reports the record as deleted until it is put back.
Text written in the forms is shared as the [Licence Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/licences.html) sets out.
The operator still acts on requests under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).
A co-author who has not agreed to these terms in a form is bound by them only as far as the law makes them so; for them, this section describes what the law already places on the authors of a work.

## What readers may do

Readers may read, download and reuse each listed work under its own licence.
The text of this site may be reused under CC BY 4.0, as set out in the [Licence Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/licences.html).

## What is not allowed

- Submitting work of which you are not an author.
- Submitting material that infringes copyright or other rights.
- Submitting personal data of third parties without a lawful basis.
- Spam, abuse, and attempts to disrupt the site or the submission process.
- Confirming in a form something that is not true, such as where the authors live or stay, the submitter's age, the agreement of the authors or the statement on generative models.

The operator may decline or remove a submission that breaks these rules.
If a confirmation turns out to be untrue, the operator removes the record under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html) as soon as the operator learns of it. From 2026-11-22, the operator may also decline further submissions from the same GitHub account or ORCID iD.
The operator relies on the confirmations in good faith and does not check them. A work listed on an untrue confirmation does not mean that Sophaxis is offered where the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) says it is not.
The confirmations stay in the public issue, so that what was confirmed, and when, can be shown.
Nothing here asks a submitter for a penalty, or for damages beyond what the law provides.

## Acts outside these rules that may come near a law

Sophaxis is run so that the operator's own acts do not meet the elements of the laws that its policies name.
A person who acts against these terms, or outside them, may still come near the elements of a law by that act.
The table lists such acts that could happen on Sophaxis, the law that each may come near, and a caution from the operator.
The table lists possible paths only. It is not complete. It does not say that a listed act is unlawful, or that an act not listed is lawful.
The articles it names are quoted at the end of this section.

| Act | Law it may come near | Caution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Submitting a version that the authors have no right to share under its licence, such as one whose publisher holds an exclusive licence | Copyright Act, Articles 21 and 23 | Submit only a version that the authors may share under its licence. Such a record is removed under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html). |
| Giving another person's ORCID iD in the form, or signing in to another person's ORCID or GitHub account to pass the identity check | Penal Code, Article 233; Act on the Prohibition of Unauthorized Computer Access, Article 3 | Use only your own iD and your own accounts. |
| Confirming the agreement of a co-author who did not agree, or confirming anything else that is not true in a form | Penal Code, Article 233; Civil Code, Article 709 | Confirm only what is true. The record is removed as soon as the operator learns of it. |
| Presenting a listing on Sophaxis as peer review or as publication in a journal, in a CV, an application for funding or an advertisement | Penal Code, Article 246; Act against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations, Article 5 | Describe a listing as what it is: a moderated listing of a preprint, which is not peer review ([Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html)). |
| Using the name Sophaxis or its logo on goods or services, or in advertising, so that they seem to come from Sophaxis or to be endorsed by it | Unfair Competition Prevention Act, Article 2(1)(i) and (ii); Act against Unjustifiable Premiums and Misleading Representations, Article 5 | Do not use the name or the logo in trade. The page [Name, logo and badge](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/brand.html) says how they may be used. |
| Reusing a PDF copy or a record beyond what its licence allows, for example without the credit that the licence asks | Copyright Act, Articles 21 and 23 | Reuse each work under its own licence, which its record page names. |
| Vouching for a submission with words that are not true, for example about where the researcher lives or stays, or about being an author | Penal Code, Article 233; Civil Code, Article 709 | Vouch only with words that are true. |
| Writing another person's personal data, or something that harms a person's reputation, in an issue, a comment or an email | Penal Code, Articles 230 and 231; Civil Code, Article 709 | Do not write it. A report of exposed personal data takes the record page offline at once, under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html). |

The responsibility for an act done against these terms, or outside them, lies with the person who did it.
Except where the law makes the operator responsible, the operator is not responsible for such acts.
This does not exclude or limit the operator's liability for loss that the operator causes by intent or negligence, which is set out under No warranty below.

<!-- text: Copyright Act 21; Copyright Act 23; Penal Code 233; Unauthorized Computer Access Act 3; Civil Code 709; Penal Code 246; Premiums and Representations Act 5; Unfair Competition Prevention Act 2; Penal Code 230; Penal Code 231 -->

## No warranty

Sophaxis is provided as it is.
It does not guarantee the quality, correctness or completeness of listed work.
It does not guarantee that the site will always be reachable.
The operator is liable, as Japanese law provides, for loss that the operator causes by intent or negligence.
The operator is not liable for loss caused only by the content of a listed work, which its authors write, or only by GitHub, Vercel or a repository, unless the law makes the operator liable for it.
Sophaxis applies Japan's Consumer Contract Act to readers and authors as if its operator were a business operator under it.

## Changes and closure

These terms and the other policies may change.
The date on each page shows its last change, and earlier versions stay in the public repository.
No change will introduce fees.

A change that takes away or narrows a right of authors or readers, or adds a duty, is announced on the top page before it takes effect, with what changes and from which date.
The announcement comes at least 14 days ahead, unless the law or an urgent problem, such as a security or legal risk, requires the change sooner.
Even then, the change is announced before it takes effect.
Each change to a policy is also entered, on the day it is published or announced, in the [feed of policy changes](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/changes.xml), which carries nothing else.
Other changes, such as clearer wording or new examples, take effect on the date the page shows, which is never before the day they are published.
A change is made only as Article 548-4 of Japan's Civil Code allows: when it is in the general interest of authors and readers, or when it is reasonable in the light of the purpose of these terms, the need for it and its content.
Silence, or continuing to use Sophaxis, is not taken as agreement to a change.
A person who does not accept a change can stop using Sophaxis, and an author can withdraw their works under the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html).

<!-- text: Civil Code 548-4 -->

## Continuity

Sophaxis is run by one person, and is planned so that it can stop without loss.

- A slow decision is not a pause: moderation can take several weeks or a few months. A pause is for when the operator cannot work on Sophaxis at all, for example because of illness. If that lasts for more than 30 days, the top page says that new submissions are paused. Listed records stay online.
- Unless the operator cannot act, a closure is announced on the top page at least 30 days ahead, and new submissions stop first.
- If Sophaxis closes, the operator will keep the repository with every record public, so that the records stay readable. Each week, the pages and the PDF copies are also saved to the Internet Archive, where every author of the work consents to it.
- The code and the records are archived at Zenodo with each release, under a DOI that resolves to the latest version: [10.5281/zenodo.24033371](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24033371).
- The operator may hand Sophaxis over to another person, to an institution or to a legal entity. A hand-over is announced on the site first, and these terms stay in force until the new operator changes them in the ordinary way.
- Anyone may copy the repository and continue the work elsewhere under its licences: CC BY 4.0 for the text and MIT for the code. Each listed work keeps its own licence.
- The DOIs stay with the repositories that issued them, whatever happens to Sophaxis.

## Law

These terms are governed by the laws of Japan.
Nothing in them limits a right that the law does not allow to be limited.
In particular, nothing in them excludes or limits liability for intent or gross negligence, or any liability that Japan's Consumer Contract Act or another law does not allow to be excluded or limited.

## Disputes

A dispute about Sophaxis or a listed work is settled by agreement wherever possible.

1. Write to the operator first, by email to the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547), or in an issue if the matter can be public. Say what the dispute is about and what would settle it.
2. Both sides then try, in good faith, to reach an agreement by talking. The operator answers within 7 days and does not leave a dispute without reply.
3. If talking does not settle it within 60 days, either side may propose mediation, such as civil conciliation (minji chotei) at a Japanese summary court, before going to court.

From 2026-11-25, if a dispute is not settled in these ways, it goes to the Utsunomiya District Court or the Utsunomiya Summary Court, as the court of first instance by agreement, for a person who has agreed to these terms in a form; this agreement is not exclusive.
Until then, the court of first instance by agreement is, on the same terms, the district court or the summary court that has jurisdiction over the operator's place of residence.
For anyone else, the court that the law sets has jurisdiction.
The operator's address is given on request, as the [Operator and contact](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.html) page says.
This does not take away a right that the law gives a consumer, or a person outside Japan, to bring or defend a case in another court.
Nothing in this section stops anyone from asking a court for urgent relief, or from using the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).

## People outside Japan

Sophaxis is run from Japan and can be read from anywhere.

- The same steps apply. Talks and mediation can be held in writing or online, in English or Japanese, so that no one has to travel to Japan to settle a dispute.
- These terms are governed by the laws of Japan. Where the law of a person's own country gives them protection that cannot be set aside by agreement, such as the protection of consumers, that protection still applies.
- A person outside Japan who may sue in the courts of their own country under that country's law keeps that right; the agreement on the court above does not take it away.
- These terms are written in English, and a Japanese translation is published. Where the translation differs from the English text, the English text applies.

## GitHub and Vercel

Sophaxis runs on two services based in the United States, and their own terms apply alongside these.

- Submitting to Sophaxis means using GitHub: opening an issue, commenting and attaching files are governed by GitHub's Terms of Service and Privacy Statement, between the user and GitHub.
- Reading Sophaxis means receiving pages from Vercel, which handles each request, including the IP address, under its own terms and privacy policy, possibly in countries other than Japan or the reader's own.
- These terms bind the operator and the people who use Sophaxis. They do not bind GitHub or Vercel, and they give no one a claim against GitHub or Vercel, or against the operator for what GitHub or Vercel does.
- A dispute with GitHub or Vercel themselves follows their terms, including their own choice of law and court. The steps in Disputes above cover only the operator and Sophaxis.
- Material in the Sophaxis repository or its issues can also be reported to GitHub through GitHub's own process, and material on the site to Vercel. The operator acts on requests under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html) whether or not GitHub or Vercel has acted.
- If GitHub or Vercel removes, limits or blocks something on their side, for example under the law of the United States, Sophaxis may not be able to restore it.

Their terms were read at their sources on 2026-11-09: GitHub's [Terms of Service](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service) (effective 2026-04-27), [Acceptable Use Policies](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/acceptable-use-policies/github-acceptable-use-policies) and [General Privacy Statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement) (effective 2026-04-27); Vercel's [Terms of Service](https://vercel.com/legal/terms) (last updated 2026-10-19), [Acceptable Use Policy](https://vercel.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy) (last updated 2026-04-21) and [Privacy Notice](https://vercel.com/legal/privacy-notice) (last updated 2026-06-01).
What they say that matters to people who use Sophaxis:

- GitHub accepts only users aged 13 or over, or older where a user's own country requires it (GitHub Terms, B.3).
- What is written or attached in an issue must follow GitHub's Acceptable Use Policies, among them its rules on spam, harassment and other people's private information (GitHub Terms, C).
- GitHub may refuse or remove content that breaks the law or its terms, and may close accounts (GitHub Terms, D.2 and M.3).
- Content in a public repository and in its issues can be seen by everyone, and GitHub's terms do not restrict its lawful use by others (GitHub Terms, D.5 and D.8). GitHub and its affiliates may store, copy and display it, and use it to train AI features and the models of their affiliates (GitHub Terms, D.4); there is no setting that turns this off for public content (GitHub Terms, J.3).
- The site is served on Vercel's free Hobby plan, which Vercel allows only for personal or non-commercial use; Sophaxis is non-commercial. Vercel may disable or remove a deployment on that plan with or without notice, so the site can go offline without warning; the records stay in the repository (Vercel Terms, section 4).
- On the Hobby plan, Vercel may use the content it serves to train AI and machine learning models, and share it with third parties for that purpose, unless the account turns this off in its team settings (Vercel Terms, section 3). The operator has not confirmed that this setting is turned off for the Sophaxis account.
- Content on the site must also follow Vercel's Acceptable Use Policy, and Vercel may remove or disable content (Vercel Terms, sections 3 and 8).
- GitHub and Vercel each provide their services "as is", without warranty, and limit their liability (GitHub Terms, O and P; Vercel Terms, sections 20 and 21). Their terms are governed by the law of California, with the courts of San Francisco, and Vercel's also provide for arbitration (GitHub Terms, S.1; Vercel Terms, section 23).

## General

- The other policies are part of these terms. Where a policy deals with a subject in more detail, it applies to that subject; otherwise, where they differ, these terms apply. The FAQ, the step-by-step page and the Disclaimer explain these terms and do not change them.
- If a part of these terms is held invalid or unenforceable, the rest stays in force, and that part applies as far as the law allows.
- If the operator does not enforce a part of these terms at one time, that does not waive it.
- From 2026-11-21, a person under 13 cannot submit.
- A person under 18 may submit only with the consent of a parent or guardian.
- Where the law gives a person who submitted as a minor a right to have the listing removed, the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html) applies.
- A notice to the operator is given by email to the address on the ORCID record, or in an issue. A notice to an author is given in their submission issue.

## Contact

The operator and every way to reach the operator are on the [Operator and contact](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.html) page.
Questions go to the [issues of the repository](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues).
Anything that should not be public goes by email to the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547).
Requests to remove material follow the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).

# Submission Policy

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [投稿の規程（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

The laws, licences and terms that this page cites are quoted at the end of each section that cites them.
Japanese statutes are quoted in full, as the e-Gov law API gives them. The other texts are quoted word for word from their official sources, as fetched on 2026-11-11, and are not translated.
A citation whose source could not be fetched is named there as not quoted, with the reason.

## Who can submit

If you are worried about your personal data because Vercel, which serves the site, or GitHub, which keeps the submissions, may use what they hold to train AI models, do not submit. The [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html) explains these uses.

Only an author of a work can submit it.
Sophaxis confirms this through ORCID, before a moderator reads the work.

- The ORCID record given in the form links to the GitHub account that opened the issue.
- The ORCID iD belongs to an author of the work: either the DOI metadata lists it for an author, or the ORCID record lists the DOI among its works and its name matches an author.

A submission that does not pass both is not listed.
The first check confirms that the person who controls the ORCID record opened the issue. It is not an official identity check.
Authors without an ORCID iD cannot submit.
From 2026-11-21, a person under 13 cannot submit.
A submitter under 18 needs the consent of a parent or guardian.
From 2026-11-22, Sophaxis does not list work by an author under 18 who lives or stays in India.
From 2027-05-13, Rule 10 of India's Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 lets the data of a person under 18 be processed only with the verifiable consent of a parent, and Sophaxis does not verify that consent.
From 2026-11-22, Sophaxis does not list work by an author who lives in any of the 28 places in the table below, or who stays in one between the submission and the listing, and the submitter confirms this in the form.
A stay counts even if it is short, such as for travel, work or study.
Stays count because the laws of several of these places reach people who are there, not only people who live there; Article 3(2) of the GDPR, for example, speaks of data subjects who are in the Union.
Sophaxis does not offer its service there, because it meets none of the duties that the law there places, or is reported to place, on a service offered to people there; the [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html) says more.
This rule depends only on where an author lives or stays, not on nationality, race, ethnic origin or any other personal characteristic.
An author of any nationality who lives elsewhere and does not stay there can submit, and an author who lives or stays there cannot, whatever their nationality.
The reasons are laws that require a local representative, the storage of personal data in the country, or registration there (among them Article 27 of the GDPR and of the UK GDPR; Article 13 of the EU Digital Services Act; Article 53 of China's Personal Information Protection Law; section 37(5) of Thailand's Personal Data Protection Act), which Sophaxis, run unpaid by one person within free services, does not have; the operator has decided not to appoint a representative, as the Privacy Policy explains.
The rule is that Sophaxis is not offered where a law requires, or is reported to require, a service offered to people there to have a representative there, to keep personal data there, to register there, or to meet conditions before personal data leaves the place that Sophaxis cannot meet.
A place is added to the list as soon as such a duty is reported, before its law has been read at its source, and it is taken off only after that law has been read at its source and found not to reach Sophaxis.
Each change to the list is announced on the top page before it takes effect, as the Terms of Use set out.
Sophaxis relies on the submitter's confirmation and does not check where authors live or stay.
If it turns out that an author lives there, or stayed there between the submission and the listing, the record is removed under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html), and the operator reviews the decision on a representative.

## What can be submitted

Sophaxis accepts work in philosophy, mathematics, logic, the philosophy of mathematics and the philosophy of science.
Work that belongs mainly to another field is out of scope, even if it uses mathematics.

The work must already be deposited in Zenodo, Figshare, OSF Preprints, SocArXiv, MetaArXiv, arXiv, Preprints.org, SSRN, Research Square, SciELO Preprints, Qeios, ScienceOpen Preprints, Advance, KC Works or Jxiv, with a DOI.
It must carry CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 1.0 in its DOI metadata, as set out in the [Licence Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/licences.html).
It must have a title, an abstract and references, in the ordinary form of a scholarly paper.

From 2026-11-23, a new work is listed only if at least six months have passed since its first DOI was registered.
The six months are counted to the day the submission issue is opened, in Japan time.
They end on the same day of the month, or on the last day of a shorter month.
The first DOI is the DOI registered earliest among the DOI given and the DOIs that its metadata names as earlier versions of the work, or as the DOI of all its versions.
In Zenodo this is the DOI of all versions, and in Figshare the DOI of the first version.
The day of registration is the one that DataCite or Crossref records.
Where the metadata gives no such day, as for Jxiv, the operator checks it by hand.
The automatic check in the issue reads these days and counts the six months.
A submission opened too early is not listed; a new issue can be opened once the six months have passed.
This does not apply to a new version of a work that Sophaxis already lists, or to a submission opened before 2026-11-23.

From 2026-11-23, a work for which Crossref records a retraction, a partial retraction, a withdrawal or a removal is not listed.
A work for which it records an expression of concern goes to the operator, who decides under the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html).
Crossref includes the data of the Retraction Watch database.
The automatic check in the issue reads these notices for the DOI given.
A notice that a repository shows only on its own page, and not to Crossref, is not seen by the check.

Work that a journal has already published may be submitted only in a version that the authors may share under such a licence.
Publishers set different terms for this.
The submitter gives the DOI of the published version in the form, as set out under "When the work is published" below.

## When a work has more than one author

From 2026-11-21, a work with more than one author is listed only after every other author confirms their own agreement.
Each confirms in one of two ways.
One is a comment in the submission issue, from a GitHub account that their ORCID record links.
The comment says "I agree to the listing of this work on Sophaxis." and gives their ORCID iD.
The automatic check in the issue counts each confirmation.
The other is an email to the operator, after which the operator confirms them through their ORCID record.
This consent covers the listing, and the provision of their personal data that the [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html) sets out.
An email confirmation says the same, and the operator's reply links the Privacy Policy.
Saving the record to the Internet Archive needs a separate consent from every author, which the form asks and which may be left empty; without it the record is not saved there.
Any author can withdraw a consent at any time, by a removal issue or by email.

## A researcher who vouches for a first submission

From 2026-11-23, a submitter who is not yet an author of a work that Sophaxis lists needs one researcher to vouch for it.
That researcher's public ORCID record lists a journal article, a book chapter or a book with a DOI, and links the GitHub account from which they comment.
The researcher comments in the submission issue with these words and their own ORCID iD: "I vouch for this submission to Sophaxis. I am not an author of this work, and I do not live in, or stay in, a place where Sophaxis is not offered."
The authors of the work and the operator cannot vouch.
Like an author, the researcher must not live in, or stay in, a place where Sophaxis is not offered.
Vouching says that the work is in scope and in the ordinary form of a scholarly paper.
It is not a review, and the moderator still decides.
The automatic check in the issue reads the researcher's public ORCID record as it reads a co-author's, and counts the vouching.
The researcher can take it back by deleting the comment before the listing.
A submitter who is already an author of a listed work needs no one to vouch, and neither does a new version of a listed work.

## What the submitter confirms

Every author of the work agrees to its listing on Sophaxis.
The authors have the right to share this version under its licence; if a journal has published the work, the publisher allows it.
The submitter confirms both, and each point below, by ticking its box in the submission form, which has the same 29 boxes, in the same words and order.
The automatic check in the issue refuses a submission unless every box of a group is ticked: the confirmations always, the consent and agreement from 2026-11-21, and where the authors live from 2026-11-22.

### Confirmations

- I confirm that I am an author of this work.
- I confirm that the ORCID iD given in this form is my own.
- I confirm that every author of this work agrees to this submission and to its listing on Sophaxis.
- I confirm that the licence given in the DOI metadata applies to the deposited version.
- I confirm that the authors have the right to share this version under that licence, and that, if a journal has published the work, the publisher allows it.
- I confirm that the work contains no material, such as figures or long quotations, that the authors may not share.
- I confirm that the work contains no personal data of third parties.
- I confirm that the statement on generative models is complete and true.
- I confirm that, from 2026-11-24, the statements on funding, competing interests, and human participants and research ethics are complete and true.
- I confirm that everything else I state in this form is true.
- I agree that the authors bear full responsibility for the work and its listing, as the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html#the-authors-bear-full-responsibility) set out.
- I agree that a listing is moderation, not peer review, and that it is not to be presented as peer review ([Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html#moderation-is-not-peer-review)).

### Consent and agreement

- I confirm that every author consents to the record being published and offered through OAI-PMH.
- I confirm that every author consents to the record being provided to GitHub, Vercel and ORCID in the United States, as the [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html#services-outside-japan) sets out.
- I confirm that every author consents to the public parts of this submission being given, for help with the review, to Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI in the United States, as the [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html#services-outside-japan) sets out.
- I agree to the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html), in their version on the day of submission.
- I agree to the settlement of disputes, and to the court named, under [Disputes](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html#disputes) in the Terms of Use.
- I agree that Sophaxis gives no warranty, as [No warranty](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html#no-warranty) in the Terms of Use sets out.
- I agree to the [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html).
- I agree to the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html).
- I agree to the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html), including how a decision can be challenged under [Decisions](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html#decisions).
- I agree to the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).
- I agree to the [Copyright Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/copyright.html).
- I agree to the [Licence Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/licences.html).
- I agree to the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html).
- I confirm that I am 13 or older, as from 2026-11-21 a person under 13 cannot submit ([Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html#general)).
- I confirm that, if I am under 18, I submit only with the consent of a parent or guardian.

### Where the authors live

- I confirm that no author of this work lives in any of the places listed above, or stays in one between the submission and the listing, even briefly (such as for travel, work or study).
- I confirm that no author under 18 lives or stays in India.

One more box, on saving the record page and the PDF copies to the Internet Archive, may be left empty; the work is listed either way.
## How to submit

1. Deposit the preprint in Zenodo, Figshare, OSF Preprints, SocArXiv, MetaArXiv, arXiv, Preprints.org, SSRN, Research Square, SciELO Preprints, Qeios, ScienceOpen Preprints, Advance, KC Works or Jxiv, under an accepted licence, and obtain its DOI.
2. Link your ORCID record to your GitHub account: add `https://github.com/<your username>` under "Websites & social links".
3. Open a submission issue in the Sophaxis repository and give the DOI, your ORCID iD, the category and the statement on generative models.
4. An automatic check reads the DOI metadata and your ORCID record, and posts the result in the issue.
5. A moderator checks the submission under the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html). If it passes, a record page is published.

The title, the authors, the abstract, the licence and the versions are taken from the DOI metadata, not typed in by hand.

The submission issue is public.
Your GitHub username and everything you write in the form will be visible to anyone.

## Language models and other generative models

Work written or developed with language models is accepted, on one condition: the use is disclosed.
The same condition applies to every other generative model, including models that produce images, figures, audio or code.

The disclosure must name the tools used and say what they were used for,
for example drafting, translation, proofs, code, literature search, editing, figures or images.
If no generative model was used, the statement says so.

From 2026-11-21, the form also asks for the extent of use, at one of four levels. The authors choose the highest level that applies:

- None: no generative model was used.
- Editing: language editing, translation or proofreading only.
- Assistance: structure, literature search or checking; the authors wrote the text.
- Drafting: a generative model drafted text, proofs, code or figures that the authors revised.

The record page shows the level the authors chose, above their statement. The level does not replace the statement; the statement still names the tools and what each did.
A level of "None" cannot stand beside a statement that names a model.

A language model cannot be listed as an author.
No other generative model can be listed as an author either.
The authors bear full responsibility for the work, as the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html) set out.

If substantial undisclosed use comes to light after listing,
the record receives a notice, and the authors are asked to add a disclosure.

## Funding, competing interests, research ethics, and data

From 2026-11-24, the form asks three statements, and a work is listed only if each is given.
The automatic check in the issue confirms that each field is filled in; it does not judge what it says.

- Funding: every funder of the work, with grant numbers, or that the work had no funding.
- Competing interests: any financial or personal interest of an author that bears on the work, such as employment, consultancy, payments or a close relation to a person the work discusses, or that there is none.
- Human participants and research ethics: whether the work involves human participants, such as surveys, interviews or experiments with people.

Work that involves human participants must name the ethics committee that approved it, or say why no approval was needed under the rules that applied where the research was done.
Every participant who can be identified must have consented, and the statement says so.
Work that contains personal data of third parties is not accepted, as set out above.

The form also asks, as an option, where the data, code and other materials on which the work rests can be found, such as a repository with a DOI, or that there are none.
Sophaxis encourages authors to make them available, but does not require it and does not check them.

The record page shows each statement as the authors give it.
Sophaxis does not check the statements beyond reading them.
A statement found to be untrue is handled under "Research integrity" in the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html).
This does not apply to a submission opened before 2026-11-24.

## Versions and updates

A work is listed once, under one Sophaxis id.
That id is never given to another work, even after a record is withdrawn or removed.

A new version is a new version in the repository.
Most repositories give each version its own DOI.
arXiv keeps one DOI for all versions, and that DOI leads to the latest one; the record then lists the same DOI with the date of each version.
Submit it as an update to the existing record; earlier versions stay listed.

## When the work is published

A listed preprint stays listed when a later version is published in a journal, in proceedings or in a book.
The record page then shows the published version at the top: what it is, where and when it appeared, and its DOI.
It asks readers to cite the published version, and it names the listed version as the preprint.

Any one author reports the published version with the [published-version form](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=published.yml), from the GitHub account that the author's ORCID record links.
An automatic check confirms that the report comes from an author, and reads the metadata of the published DOI.
The published version must be a journal article, a conference paper, a book chapter or a book.
It must not be in one of the accepted repositories, and it must share an author with the record.
A moderator then records it, and the decision is public in the issue.
A published version can also be given at submission, and the same checks run on it.

Sophaxis does not judge the peer review of a journal.
The record repeats what the authors state: that the published version was peer-reviewed, that it was not, or nothing.
It also says whether the publisher's metadata links the published version to the preprint, or whether only an author reported it.

Each week Sophaxis looks in the metadata of Crossref and DataCite for a published version that is linked to a listed preprint and shares an author with it.
It records nothing by itself: it asks the authors to report it.
The same weekly check confirms that a recorded published version still resolves.
When the publisher adds a retraction, a correction or another notice to the published version, the record page shows it.

Some publishers ask authors to remove or change a preprint on publication.
The authors check the publisher's terms.
If the listing must go, any one author can withdraw it under the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html), and the record page keeps the link to the published version.

## Examples of what is not accepted

These examples show how the rules above apply. They are not a complete list; the rules decide.
Each group matches a reason that a moderator names when declining, under the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html).

Authorship: the submitter must be an author, and every author must agree.

- Submitting a colleague's paper for them, even with their permission. Only an author can submit.
- Submitting a paper by a teacher, a supervisor or a famous author because it deserves to be read.
- Opening the issue from a GitHub account that the ORCID record does not link to, such as a lab account or a second personal account.
- Giving the ORCID iD of a co-author, or of anyone other than the person who opens the issue.
- Giving an ORCID iD that neither the DOI metadata nor the ORCID record connects to the work.
- Submitting a work when a co-author has not agreed, or has said no.
- Opening a new GitHub account to submit a declined work again under another name.

Repository and DOI: the work must have its own DOI from an accepted repository.

- A PDF on a personal website, a university page, Google Drive, Dropbox, Academia.edu or ResearchGate.
- A work on PhilArchive, PhilSci-Archive or HAL alone, which give no DOI of their own. Deposit it also in an accepted repository.
- The DOI of the version a journal published, given as the DOI of the deposit.
- A different work given as the published version of a listed preprint.
- The DOI of an article in a SciELO journal, rather than in SciELO Preprints.
- The DOI of a peer review report, as Qeios and ScienceOpen also register.
- A DOI that does not resolve, or that leads to a different work.

Licence: the DOI metadata must carry CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 1.0.

- CC BY-NC 4.0, CC BY-ND 4.0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 or CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
- CC BY 3.0, CC BY 2.0 or any other earlier version of a Creative Commons licence.
- The arXiv non-exclusive licence (arXiv.org perpetual, non-exclusive license).
- "All rights reserved", or no licence in the DOI metadata at all.
- A licence written only in the PDF or on the repository page, but not in the DOI metadata.
- A licence changed after listing to one that is not accepted. The weekly check reports it, and the operator looks into it.

Scope: the work must belong mainly to philosophy, mathematics, logic, the philosophy of mathematics or the philosophy of science.

- A paper in physics, economics, computer science, engineering, biology or psychology that uses mathematics as a tool.
- A machine-learning benchmark, a software description or a data set.
- Literary criticism, history or political commentary that does not argue a philosophical or mathematical question.
- Self-help or spiritual guidance that gives advice or practice instead of arguing a philosophical question, or a political manifesto or campaign.

Form: the work must have a title, an abstract and references, in the ordinary form of a scholarly paper.

- Slides, a poster, lecture notes or a recorded talk.
- A blog post or an essay without references.
- An abstract alone, or a title page without the full text.
- Several unrelated papers in one deposit.
- Fiction, poetry or a diary.

Disclosure: the statement on generative models must name the tools and say what they were used for.

- "None" when a language model drafted, translated or edited any part of the text.
- A statement that says only that a language model was used, without naming the tool or saying what it did.
- Figures or images made with a generative model that the statement leaves out.
- A language model or another generative model listed as an author in the DOI metadata or in the paper.

Rights or personal data: the authors must be free to share everything in the work, and it must not expose others.

- A figure, a table or a photograph copied from a book, a paper or a website without permission, beyond what quotation allows. Citing the source does not replace permission.
- The publisher's typeset version of a journal article, when the publisher allows only the authors' manuscript to be shared.
- Names, email addresses, postal addresses or photographs of private persons who have not agreed.
- Survey or interview answers from which a participant can be identified.
- Screenshots of private messages, emails or chats.
- Unpublished material of another researcher, shared without their consent.

Spam or abuse.

- The same work submitted again and again, or under several titles.
- Many submissions opened at once to flood the issues.
- Advertising, links to paid services, or text written to sell something.
- Text that harasses, threatens or defames a named person.
- Attempts to break the form, the automatic check or the site, for example by placing code or markup in the fields.
- Pretending to be another person, an institution or a journal.

Versions.

- A new version submitted as a new work, instead of as an update to the existing Sophaxis id.
- A new version of a withdrawn record. A withdrawn record takes no new versions.

## Withdrawal

Any one author can withdraw a listed work under the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html).
Records are not deleted: a withdrawn work keeps its record page with a withdrawal notice, so that citations to it do not break.
An author can instead have the record removed, so that only its Sophaxis id stays.
Removal for legal reasons follows the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html

# Moderation Policy

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [モデレーションの規程（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

The laws, licences and terms that this page cites are quoted at the end of each section that cites them.
Japanese statutes are quoted in full, as the e-Gov law API gives them. The other texts are quoted word for word from their official sources, as fetched on 2026-11-11, and are not translated.
A citation whose source could not be fetched is named there as not quoted, with the reason.

## Moderation is not peer review

Acceptance is moderation, not peer review.
Moderation decides whether a submission may be listed.
It does not judge whether the work is correct, original or important.

## What moderation checks

- The automatic check has verified the submitter and the licence.
- The work is in scope.
- The DOI resolves to the work described, and the submitter is one of its authors.
- The work carries one of the accepted licences: CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 1.0.
- The work has a title, an abstract and references, in the ordinary form of a scholarly paper. Where the repository lets Sophaxis fetch the PDF, the automatic check reads its shape (the number of pages, whether its text can be read, and whether the title, an abstract and references can be found) and shows it in the issue. The shape decides nothing; the moderator reads the PDF.
- The submission includes a statement on the use of language models and other generative models.
- From 2026-11-24, the submission states the funding, the competing interests, and whether the work involves human participants, with the ethics approval and the consent where it does, as the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) sets out.
- The submitter has confirmed that every author agrees and that the version may be shared.
- From 2026-11-21, every other author of a work with more than one author has confirmed their own agreement, as the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) sets out.
- From 2026-11-23, a researcher has vouched for a first submission, as the Submission Policy sets out.
- The work is not spam, not abusive and does not expose personal data of third parties.
- The work shows no affiliation or address of an author in a place where Sophaxis is not offered, as the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) lists them. If it does, the moderator asks the submitter where that author lives and whether they have stayed there since the submission, and declines the submission unless the author lives elsewhere and has not stayed there.
- The PDF carries no notice of rights that contradicts the licence in the DOI metadata, such as a publisher's "all rights reserved". If it does, the submission is declined.

## What moderation does not check

It does not check proofs, arguments or data.
It does not run plagiarism checks.
A moderator who finds plagiarism declines the submission, as set out under "Research integrity" below.
It does not check the statements on funding, competing interests, research ethics, or data and code, beyond reading them.
It does not compare the work with the literature.

## Provisional registration

A submission that passes the automatic check is provisionally registered: its issue is labelled `verified`, and it waits for a moderator.
A provisionally registered work is not on the site. It has no record page, is not offered through OAI-PMH, and is not sent to the Internet Archive or to any other service that keeps records.
Provisional registration is not acceptance. It ends when a moderator accepts or declines the submission.

## Decisions

A moderator accepts or declines a submission in its issue, and labels the issue `accepted` or `declined`.
Every decision stays public in its issue.
To help the review, the operator gives the public parts of a submission (the issue, the DOI metadata and the abstract) to three language models, Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Grok (xAI), and compares what they point out.
The operator does this by hand, in the chat of each service; no submission is sent to them automatically, and they are given nothing that is not already public.
The models only assist. No model accepts or declines a submission; every decision is taken by the operator, or by a moderator, who reads the submission.
What a model points out is given as a reason for a decision only after the operator has checked it.
As a guide, a decision can come on the day of submission, but it can also take several weeks or a few months.
Each January, the decisions of the year before are counted from the public issues and the records, with the reasons named for declining and the days to a decision, and the operator records them on the [Decisions by year](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/decisions.html) page.
The counts of the current year can be recorded before it ends, marked with the day they were counted.

A moderator who declines a submission names one or more of these reasons, with a short explanation:

- Out of scope: the work belongs mainly to a field outside philosophy, mathematics, logic, the philosophy of mathematics and the philosophy of science.
- Not in the form of a scholarly paper: it lacks a title, an abstract or references.
- Licence: the DOI metadata does not carry an accepted licence.
- Authorship: the submitter could not be confirmed as an author, or not every author agrees.
- Disclosure: the statement on generative models is missing or does not say how they were used, or, from 2026-11-24, a statement on funding, competing interests, or human participants and research ethics is missing or incomplete.
- Rights or personal data: the work contains material that the authors may not share, or personal data of third parties, or the PDF carries a notice of rights that contradicts its licence.
- Plagiarism: the work presents the words, ideas, proofs or results of others as the authors' own, or presents the authors' own earlier work as new, without saying where they come from.
- Where the authors live or stay: an author lives in a place where Sophaxis is not offered, or stayed in one between the submission and the listing.
- Spam or abuse.

The submitter can answer in the issue.
The operator then looks at the submission once more, and that decision is final.
The submitter can also go to a court, or to an out-of-court dispute settlement body certified under Article 21 of the Digital Services Act.

<!-- text: DSA 21 -->

## Moderators

The operator is at present the only moderator.
Other moderators may be invited.
A researcher in these fields who would like to moderate can write to the operator; the operator decides whom to invite.
Each is named, with an ORCID iD, on the [Operator and contact](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.html) page before taking any decision, and moderates under this policy without pay.
A second moderator is invited only when all of these hold:

- They have an ORCID iD and a published or listed work in one of the fields of Sophaxis.
- They agree, in a public issue, to moderate under this policy without pay.
- They declare their interests as an adviser does, and the contact page shows the declaration.
- No work of theirs has been declined or removed under "Research integrity" below.

A moderator does not decide on their own work, or on the work of a close collaborator; another moderator, or the operator, decides it.
When two moderators disagree, the operator decides, and says so in the issue.
A moderator may stop at any time, and the operator may end a moderator's role; either is recorded on the contact page with the date.
Since 2026-11-10 the operator has also invited researchers to form an advisory board, which advises on the policies and decides no submission; the call is on [Advisory board: a call](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/advisory.html).

## Conflicts of interest

Submissions by the operator are moderated under the same rules and are marked on their record pages.
The automatic check applies to them without exception.
While the operator is the only moderator, the operator also decides on their own submissions; the mark on the record page says so.
Once there is another moderator, no moderator decides on their own submission or on one by a close collaborator.
The operator's own submissions get no priority: they are moderated in the order they come, and their records have no other place on the site than any other record.
From 2026-11-09, a submission by the operator is listed no sooner than seven days after its submission issue is opened, so that anyone can object in the issue first.
The record keeps the day the issue was opened, and the build of the site refuses a record listed sooner.
The [Statistics](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/stats.html) page and `llms.txt` say how many of the records shown are the operator's own.

## Research integrity

Plagiarism is presenting the words, ideas, proofs or results of others as one's own, without saying where they come from.
Presenting the authors' own earlier work as new, without citing it, is treated the same way, and so is submitting one work to Sophaxis twice under different DOIs.
Quoting, paraphrasing or building on the work of others with a clear citation is not plagiarism.
Sophaxis runs no software to detect plagiarism.
A moderator who finds it in a submission declines the submission, naming "Plagiarism".

Research misconduct includes plagiarism, fabrication (making up data, results or sources), falsification (changing them so that the work misrepresents them), and an untrue statement in the form.
Anyone can raise a concern about a listed record, in public through the correction issue linked on its page.
A concern that should not be public, or that names a person, goes by email to the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547).
The operator handles a concern by the steps that COPE, the Committee on Publication Ethics, recommends for journals, as far as one person can; Sophaxis is not a member of COPE.

- The operator reads the concern and, if it concerns a listed record and is not plainly without ground, gives the authors 14 days to answer it.
- Sophaxis does not investigate misconduct. It has no power to examine data, records or witnesses. Where the research was done at an institution, or a journal has published the work, the operator tells the person who raised the concern that the institution or the journal is the body that investigates, and may inform it.
- A note is added to the record only for what is established: what the authors confirm, what an institution or a journal finds, or what a notice that Crossref records says. The note says what was found and by whom, and the day; it does not repeat an allegation.
- Where plagiarism or another problem is established, the authors are asked to correct the work in its repository or to withdraw it under the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html). Copying that infringes copyright is removed under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).
- The person who raised a concern by email is not named to the authors or to anyone else without their consent, unless the law requires it.
- A concern about a work by the operator follows the same steps, and the operator's answer is posted in the record's correction issue.

The operator closes without action a concern that is plainly made to harass, and says so to the person who raised it.

## After listing

The moderator may put a listed record in one or more [collections](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/collections.html) by topic, beside its fields.
A collection says nothing of the quality of a work, and an author can ask, in the record's correction issue, for a record to be put in a collection or taken out of one.

Corrections are added to the record as dated notes.
Anyone can report an error in a record through the link on its page, which opens a public correction issue.
The notes do not replace the work.
A record can receive a notice when a problem comes to light, such as undisclosed use of generative models.

Each week, an automatic check confirms that every listed DOI still resolves and still carries the licence in the record.
The same check reads the notices that Crossref records against each DOI of a record shown: retractions, withdrawals, removals, expressions of concern and corrections, including those from Retraction Watch.
The operator adds a new notice to the record, where its page shows it with a link, and reviews the listing.
A problem is reported in a public issue, and the operator looks into it.

## Changes to the criteria

The criteria for listing are those of the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) and of this policy: who can submit, what can be submitted, what moderation checks, and the examples of what is not accepted.
They change only as "Changes and closure" in the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html) allows, as every other policy does.

- They are reviewed at least once a year, in the yearly audit on 30 October, the day Sophaxis began, and also when a law, a repository or a service that Sophaxis relies on changes.
- A change that narrows what can be listed, or adds a duty for authors, is announced on the top page at least 14 days before it takes effect, with what changes and from which date.
- A change that only widens what can be listed, or makes the wording clearer, takes effect on the date the policy shows, which is never before the day it is published.
- Each change is entered in the [feed of policy changes](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/changes.xml) on the day it is published or announced, and in the [news](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/news.html) when it changes what an author has to do.
- The reasons for a change are given in its pull request in the public repository.

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/copyright.html

# Copyright Policy

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [著作権の規程（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/copyright.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

The laws, licences and terms that this page cites are quoted at the end of each section that cites them.
Japanese statutes are quoted in full, as the e-Gov law API gives them. The other texts are quoted word for word from their official sources, as fetched on 2026-11-11, and are not translated.
A citation whose source could not be fetched is named there as not quoted, with the reason.

## Authors keep their copyright

Sophaxis asks for no transfer of copyright and no exclusive licence.
The work stays under the licence the authors gave it in the repository.

## What Sophaxis copies, and on what basis

Titles, author names, licences and dates come from the DOI metadata, which DataCite and Crossref make openly available for reuse; for Jxiv, they come from the public metadata of JaLC.
The abstract is part of the work.
It is shown under the work's own licence, with its authors and a link to the work.

Sophaxis keeps an unmodified copy of the PDF of each listed version, so that search engines can index the full text.
It copies the file only from a repository that lets a script fetch it: Zenodo, Figshare, arXiv and Research Square.
Where the repository publishes a checksum, the copy must match it.
When a deposit holds more than one PDF, Sophaxis does not guess which one is the paper, and makes no copy.
For any other repository, the authors can attach the deposited PDF to their submission issue.
Sophaxis then keeps that file unmodified, and the record says that the authors provided it.
Without such a file, the record links to the repository only.
A copy is kept only if the file is at most 20 MB, and only while all the copies together stay within 1 GB.
A larger file stays at its repository, and the record links to it.

The copy is the file the authors deposited, shared under the work's own licence, with its authors, its licence and a link to the original.
The accepted licences allow this.
Authors can ask for the copy to be removed; the record then links to the repository only.

Each week, Sophaxis asks the Internet Archive to save its pages and the PDF copies, where every author of the work consents to it, so that they stay readable even if this site goes away.

Every record page carries the citation tags that Google Scholar reads.
Sophaxis does not control whether or when a search engine indexes a page.

## How Sophaxis meets the licences

Sophaxis shares a listed work only under the work's own licence, and only as that licence allows.
The three accepted licences permit copying and sharing for any purpose.
CC BY 4.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0 require credit; CC0 1.0 does not, but Sophaxis credits the authors anyway.

- Credit: every record page names the authors and the title, names the licence with a link to it, and links to the work by its DOI.
- No changes: the PDF copy is the deposited file, byte for byte, with every notice it carries. The abstract is shown as plain text, with formatting tags removed and its words unchanged.
- No added terms: Sophaxis adds no condition and no technical measure that would restrict what the licence allows readers to do.
- No endorsement: nothing on Sophaxis says or suggests that the authors endorse Sophaxis or its use of their work.

<!-- text: CC BY 4.0 3; CC BY 4.0 2 -->

## Work published in a journal

When a journal publishes a work, the copyright or an exclusive licence may pass to the publisher.
The authors must then make sure that the version they deposited may be shared under its licence.
If it may not, the work cannot be listed.

## Material from others

Figures, tables, long quotations and other material from others need permission, or must be used in a way the law allows, such as quotation.
The authors are responsible for this.

## Examples of what is not allowed

These examples show how this policy applies. They are not a complete list.

The version that is shared:

- Depositing the publisher's typeset version under CC BY when the copyright went to the publisher. The authors can no longer license it.
- Depositing an accepted manuscript before the embargo that the publisher sets has ended.
- Attaching to the submission issue a PDF that differs from the deposited file, such as a newer draft, an edited copy or the journal layout. The copy must be the deposited file, unmodified.
- Asking Sophaxis to change its PDF copy. A change is a new version in the repository.

Material from others:

- A figure, a table, a map or a photograph copied from a book, a paper or a website without permission, beyond quotation.
- A long passage of another work, quoted at a length that the law of quotation does not cover.
- The full text of a poem, a song or a short story by someone else.
- A translation of someone else's paper, deposited as the authors' own work, or without the permission of the original's rights holder.
- Images from an archive whose terms forbid publishing them again.
- Material under a NonCommercial or NoDerivatives licence, placed inside a work that carries CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 1.0 as though it were under that licence.
- A screenshot of software, a web page or a video, reproduced beyond what quotation allows.

Requests:

- Repeating the infringing material itself in a public removal issue. Describe where it is instead.
- Asking Sophaxis to remove a deposit from its repository. Sophaxis cannot; the request goes to the repository.

## Infringement

A rights holder who believes that a listed work infringes their rights can ask for its removal under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/licences.html

# Licence Policy

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [ライセンスの規程（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/licences.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

## Accepted licences

Sophaxis lists only work under one of these licences:

- CC BY 4.0
- CC BY-SA 4.0
- CC0 1.0

They let Sophaxis show the abstract and keep a copy of the PDF, with credit to the authors.
They also let readers reuse the work freely.
Licences with NonCommercial or NoDerivatives terms are not accepted.

## Where the licence must appear

The licence must appear in the DOI metadata of the deposit; the automatic check reads it there.
The licence condition applies in every repository.
On arXiv, choose CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 1.0 when you submit; the arXiv non-exclusive licence is not accepted.
Work on SSRN is accepted only if it carries one of the accepted licences.

## Licences of this site

The text of this site is licensed under CC BY 4.0.
The code is licensed under MIT.
Each listed work keeps its own licence.

The record data in `feed.xml`, `papers.json` and the OAI-PMH interface may be reused freely.
Abstracts in them keep the licence of their work.

## Text written in the forms

From 2026-11-21, an abstract given in a form is shared under the licence of the work.
From 2026-11-21, other text written in the forms, such as the statement on generative models, a reason for withdrawal or a correction, is shared under CC0 1.0 by the person who writes it.
This lets Sophaxis show it with the record, and lets others reuse it with the record data.
Text written in the forms before 2026-11-21 is shown with the record by the permission its writer gave by writing it in a public form for the record; anyone who wrote it can ask for it to be removed under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html

# Privacy Policy

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [個人情報の取り扱いについて](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.ja.html), which follows the headings of Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information.

The laws, licences and terms that this page cites are quoted at the end of each section that cites them.
Japanese statutes are quoted in full, as the e-Gov law API gives them. The other texts are quoted word for word from their official sources, as fetched on 2026-11-11, and are not translated.
A citation whose source could not be fetched is named there as not quoted, with the reason.

## Who handles personal data

The operator of Sophaxis, Takuya Nemoto, handles it.
The operator's address is not published; it is given on request, without delay.
Sophaxis applies Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information in full, as if its operator were a business operator under that Act.

## Purposes

Personal data is used only for these purposes:

- to confirm that a person who submits, withdraws or reports a published version, or a co-author who confirms their agreement, is an author of the work;
- from 2026-11-23, to confirm that a researcher who vouches for a first submission is not an author of the work and has a journal article, a book chapter or a book;
- to publish record pages, author pages, the lists and the search;
- to offer the records for reuse in `feed.xml`, `papers.json` and the OAI-PMH interface at `/oai`;
- to check the listed DOIs and licences each week, and, for works whose authors consent to it, to save the pages and the PDF copies to the Internet Archive each week and when they change;
- to tell search engines which addresses are new, changed or removed;
- to answer requests to withdraw, correct or remove a record, and requests about personal data;
- to serve the site, and to find and fix faults from Vercel's request logs;
- to answer questions, complaints, disputes and security reports.

## The site

The Sophaxis site sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads nothing from other servers.
Its pages contain no code or tag that sends information about a reader to anyone else, so nothing falls under the rules of Japan's Telecommunications Business Act on sending users' information outside (Article 27-12).
The search page runs one script, served by Sophaxis itself.
It reads the list of records from Sophaxis and searches it in your browser, and it sends nothing anywhere.
No other page runs a script.

Each record page has share links to X, Bluesky, Facebook, LinkedIn and email.
They are plain links to each service's own page.
Nothing is sent anywhere until a reader follows one, and the service then works under its own privacy policy.

The site is hosted on Vercel.
Vercel processes each request, including the IP address, in order to serve the page, under its own privacy policy.
Sophaxis has not turned on Vercel's analytics.
No page, a record page included, shows a count of views or downloads, and Sophaxis keeps no such count: it runs no analytics that would make one, and it does not count readers from Vercel's request logs.

<!-- text: Telecommunications Business Act 27-12 -->

## Submissions

Submissions are public GitHub issues and are subject to GitHub's terms.
Your GitHub username and everything you write in the form become public.

When a submission issue is opened or edited, a GitHub Action reads two kinds of public data.
It reads the metadata of the DOI from DataCite, Crossref or JaLC (Japan Link Center).
It reads the name, the websites and the works of the ORCID record given in the form.
It uses them only for the checks, and writes nothing else from the ORCID record anywhere.
The same check runs when a withdrawal issue or a published-version issue is opened or edited.
The check asks ORCID only for the personal details (the name), the websites and the works sections of the record.
It does not ask for the person section as a whole, so public email addresses and the country are never received.
The check uses only the name, the websites and the works, and keeps or writes nothing else from the ORCID record.
The automatic comment in a submission issue repeats the draft record, which is public already.
From 2026-11-21, a co-author who confirms their agreement in a comment gives their ORCID iD there, and the check reads their public ORCID record in the same way.
From 2026-11-23, a researcher who vouches for a first submission in a comment gives their ORCID iD there, and the check reads the name, the websites and the works of their public ORCID record in the same way. Their GitHub username, ORCID iD and comment are public in the issue, by their own act.

Giving an ORCID iD, and opening the issue from a GitHub account that the ORCID record links, are needed to submit, withdraw or report a published version.
Without them the check cannot confirm the author, and the request cannot go ahead by issue; it can still go by email, as each policy says.
Nothing else is asked of anyone.

## Records

A record holds the title, the names and ORCID iDs of the authors, the abstract, the licence, the DOIs and dates of the versions, and the statement on generative models.
Most of a record comes from the metadata of the deposit.
The statement on generative models, an abstract given in the form, a reason for withdrawal and notes on corrections come from the issues, where they are public already.
A record also gives the number of its submission issue, which shows the submitter's GitHub username.
Sophaxis keeps records without a time limit, so that citations do not break.
The issues, with the GitHub usernames in them, stay as long as GitHub keeps them; removing a record empties the issues that name it, and the operator then deletes them.
Vercel keeps its request logs for the period its service sets, and the operator does not copy them.
A removed record keeps only its Sophaxis id and the day of removal, as the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html) sets out.
Earlier versions stay in the history of the public repository and in the saves of the Internet Archive; the operator asks GitHub and the Internet Archive to remove them.

## Reuse and copies elsewhere

The records are offered for reuse in `feed.xml`, `papers.json` and the OAI-PMH interface at `/oai`.
Harvesters, such as OpenAIRE, copy the title, the authors, the abstract and the licence from there.
The OAI-PMH interface gives an email address made for harvesters, because the protocol requires one.
Requests about personal data go to the address on the operator's ORCID record, as below.
The pages and the PDF copies of a work whose authors consent to it are saved to the Internet Archive.
Works deposited at Zenodo can also be gathered in the Sophaxis community at Zenodo, https://zenodo.org/communities/sophaxis.
An author submits the record there, and Zenodo, run by CERN in Switzerland, holds it.
Sophaxis copies nothing from the community, and the operator does not change the records in it.
A request to add the record of a work by an author who lives in a place where Sophaxis is not offered, as the Submission Policy lists them, or who stayed in one between the submission and the listing, is declined from 2026-11-22, because such a work is not listed on Sophaxis; the request itself stays with Zenodo, under CERN's own terms.
When a record changes, its address is sent to search engines through IndexNow; only the address is sent.
Copies that others have already taken are outside Sophaxis's control.

## Services outside Japan

Sophaxis uses these services outside Japan: GitHub (United States) to receive submissions and keep the records, Vercel (United States) to serve the site, DataCite (Germany) and Crossref (United States) for DOI metadata, ORCID (United States) for public ORCID records, and the Internet Archive (United States) to save the pages and the PDF copies. OpenAlex (United States) is asked how it holds a listed work, by its DOI only, never about a person. Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI (all United States) receive, while a submission is reviewed, its public parts (the issue, the DOI metadata and the abstract), which the operator gives by hand to their language models, Claude, ChatGPT and Grok, to help the review; nothing is given to them after a work is listed.
Sophaxis treats the personal data in records that reaches GitHub, Vercel, ORCID and the Internet Archive, and the public parts of a submission that reach Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI while it is reviewed, as provided to a third party in a foreign country, under Article 28 of Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information.
The submission form asks for each author's consent to this, after giving the information below; the confirmation is required from 2026-11-21.
Until then, the operator lists a work by an author other than the operator only after every author has given this consent in the submission issue.
Consent to the Internet Archive is asked in a box of its own, which may be left empty; a record without it is not saved there, and `robots.txt` asks the Internet Archive not to collect it.
Any author can withdraw either consent at any time, by a removal issue or by email, and what was done before the withdrawal stays lawful.
Withdrawing the consent to the Internet Archive stops the saves without review, once the operator confirms that the request comes from an author; the operator then asks the Internet Archive to exclude the earlier copies.
Withdrawing the consent to GitHub, Vercel and ORCID removes the record, because Sophaxis cannot list a work without them.

The countries:

- The United States has no general federal law on personal data; some states have their own laws. There is no single authority for personal data across the country, and the rights a person has over their data depend on the state and the sector.
- Germany is in the European Union, where the General Data Protection Regulation applies.
- Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission publishes information on the systems of other countries.

What each service does to protect personal data is set out in its own statement:

- GitHub: [GitHub General Privacy Statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement). GitHub says it complies with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.
- Vercel: [Vercel Privacy Notice](https://vercel.com/legal/privacy-notice). Vercel says it complies with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.
- ORCID: [ORCID Privacy Policy](https://info.orcid.org/privacy-policy/). ORCID says its practices are assessed each year against the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.
- Crossref: [Crossref privacy](https://www.crossref.org/operations-and-sustainability/privacy/).
- The Internet Archive: [Terms of Use](https://archive.org/about/terms). It receives only the public pages and PDF copies, which hold no personal data beyond what the records already publish. Sophaxis cannot give information on the measures the Internet Archive takes to protect personal data: its terms can be read only with a script running, and no other statement of those measures was found.

For GitHub, Vercel and ORCID, a transfer from the European Union rests on the European Commission's adequacy decision for the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, as far as each is certified under it.

Two uses of the records by GitHub and Vercel themselves come with their terms, which Sophaxis cannot change:
