- GitHub's Terms of Service let GitHub and its affiliates use what is posted in issues and public repositories, the records among it, to train AI features and the models of its affiliates (section D.4). There is no setting that turns this off for public content (section J.3).
- Vercel's Terms of Service let Vercel, on the free Hobby plan on which Sophaxis is served, use the content of the site, the records among it, to train AI and machine learning models, and share it with third parties for that purpose, unless the account turns this off in its team settings (section 3). The operator has not confirmed that this setting is turned off for the Sophaxis account.

If these uses make you worry about your personal data, do not submit, and do not agree to be listed as an author, because Sophaxis cannot list a work without GitHub and Vercel. An author of a listed work can withdraw the consent at any time, and the record is then removed, as set out above.

Requests sent by email reach the operator's mailbox at Apple (iCloud Mail, United States), and are kept there only as long as needed to answer them and to show the answer.
What Apple says about its own measures is in the [Apple Privacy Policy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/).
A person in the European Union who writes reaches the operator in Japan, for which the European Commission has made an adequacy decision, and the mailbox at Apple in the United States; Apple says that its international transfers of personal data collected in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland are governed by Standard Contractual Clauses.

Vercel keeps request logs for Sophaxis, including the IP address.
The operator can see them, and uses them only to find and fix faults.

Apple, for the mailbox, and Vercel, for its request logs, handle personal data for Sophaxis, and neither is bound by contract not to handle it.
As the Personal Information Protection Commission's Q&A 7-53 reads Japan's Act, Sophaxis therefore treats both as entrusted with that handling, and supervises them under Article 25 of the Act.
Each publishes the measures it takes: Vercel in Schedule 2 of its [Data Processing Addendum](https://vercel.com/legal/dpa), Apple in its Privacy Policy.
Each week, an automatic step reads the date of the last update of Vercel's and Apple's privacy statements; a new date opens an issue, and the operator reads the statement again and decides whether the service can still be used.

<!-- text: APPI 28; GitHub Terms D.4; GitHub Terms J.3; Vercel Terms 3; APPI 25 -->

## Security

Records are built only from information that is public already.
The automatic checks keep nothing from an ORCID record except the name, the websites and the works.
The automatic checks run with the least permissions they need.
Only the operator can change the records, except that the automatic step of the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html) takes the record page (its title, authors, abstract and PDF copy) offline when a removal issue reports exposure of personal data.
If personal data leaks in a way that the law requires to be reported, the operator reports it to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission and tells the people concerned.
A leak must be reported when it involves sensitive personal information, data whose misuse could cause financial loss, data leaked through an act done for an improper purpose, such as an attack on the operator's accounts, or the data of more than 1,000 people.
The operator reports promptly after learning of it, and gives the full report within 30 days, or within 60 days when the leak may come from an act done for an improper purpose.

The measures, under the headings that Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission uses:

- Organisation: one person, the operator, handles personal data and answers for it. Every change to the records is a public commit or pull request.
- People: no one else handles personal data for Sophaxis. Before a moderator is invited, the operator writes here what personal data a moderator may handle and how the operator supervises it.
- Physical: Sophaxis has no servers or papers of its own. The records live in the GitHub repository and the site on Vercel.
- Technical: the automatic steps hold no key but the token GitHub gives each run, with the least permissions they need. Earlier versions of the site on Vercel are not open to the public. The operator's GitHub account, the only one that can change the repository, uses two-factor authentication. The operator signs in to Vercel, which serves the site, through that GitHub account.
- The countries where data is kept: as set out under "Services outside Japan" above.

## Automated processing

The automatic checks compare public records and post the result in the issue. They make no decision about a person.
No decision with legal or similarly significant effects on a person is made solely by automated means.
The language models that help the review make no decision; every decision on a submission is taken by a person, as the Moderation Policy sets out.
One step acts before the operator decides: when a removal issue reports exposure of personal data, it takes the record page (its title, authors, abstract and PDF copy) offline. It protects the person concerned, and is undone if the request is not upheld.
Every automatic step is listed on the page [What runs by itself](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/automation.html).

## Your choices

An author can withdraw a work, have its record removed so that only the Sophaxis id stays, or ask for the PDF copy to be removed.
A person whose personal data appears in a record can ask for its removal under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).
A person can ask for access to, correction of, suspension of the use of, or deletion of their personal data held by Sophaxis, through a removal issue that names only the Sophaxis id and the kind of request, or by email to the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547).
A person can also ask to be told the purposes for which their data is used, to have its use restricted while its accuracy or an objection is checked, and to have its provision to third parties stopped.
While a restriction lasts, the operator takes the part concerned offline.
The submission issue, with its consent, and the history of the record in the public repository are the record of provision to third parties (Article 29 of Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information); a person can ask to see what concerns them.
A person whose data is not in a record, such as a GitHub username in an issue or an IP address in Vercel's logs, writes by email.
Before answering a request about personal data, the operator confirms who is asking, through the ORCID record or by email.
A request can also be made through an agent, such as a parent or guardian or a person the requester appoints; the operator then confirms the agent's authority as well as the person's identity.
A copy of personal data is sent by email, in a commonly used electronic form, or by another method the person asks for, and never in an issue.
The operator aims to answer within 7 days.
A request about personal data is answered within one month at the latest.
If a request needs more time, the operator says so within that month, with the reasons, and answers within three months of the request.
When the operator does not act on a request about personal data, it says why within one month.
It also says that the person can complain to a data protection authority and can go to court.
On request, the operator tells a person which recipients were told of a correction, a removal or a restriction of their data.
Requests cost nothing.
A complaint about how personal data is handled goes to the same email address.
A person can also consult Japan's [Personal Information Protection Commission](https://www.ppc.go.jp/).
A person in Switzerland can also complain to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner.

These rights are open to everyone, wherever they live.
Where a person's own law gives them more rights over their personal data, such as the General Data Protection Regulation in the European Union, the operator honours those rights as far as they apply to Sophaxis.
Personal data that GitHub or Vercel hold about their own users, such as GitHub accounts, is theirs to handle under their own privacy statements; a request about it goes to them.

<!-- text: APPI 29 -->

## The right to object

Anyone can object, at any time, to the use of their personal data on Sophaxis, on grounds of their own situation.
An objection goes by a removal issue or by email.
After an objection, the operator stops the use objected to, unless it shows compelling legitimate grounds that override the person's interests, rights and freedoms, or the data is needed for legal claims.
The operator gives those grounds in writing.

## People in the European Union and the United Kingdom

From 2026-11-22, Sophaxis does not offer its service to people in the European Union, the European Economic Area or the United Kingdom.
It does not list work by an author who lives there, or who stays there between the submission and the listing, even briefly, and the submission form asks the submitter to confirm it.
This depends only on where an author lives or stays, not on nationality, race, ethnic origin or any other personal characteristic.
Anyone can read the site, but Sophaxis does not direct itself to people there.
The operator therefore considers that the General Data Protection Regulation and the UK GDPR do not reach Sophaxis under Article 3(2).
The rights in this section are honoured all the same, as far as they apply.
For people in the European Union and the United Kingdom, the basis for this use is a legitimate interest: checking who the authors are, keeping a public scholarly record, serving the site safely, and answering the people who write.
Records are kept to preserve the scholarly record, for freedom of expression and information (Article 17(3)(a)).
Where a transfer outside the European Union has no adequacy decision or other safeguard, as for the Internet Archive, it rests on the author's explicit consent (Article 49(1)(a)).
The possible risks of that transfer, of which the consent is given knowing: Sophaxis knows of no adequacy decision or other safeguard that covers the Internet Archive, so personal data saved there may be protected less than under the General Data Protection Regulation, and a person may find it harder to enforce their rights there.
That consent is asked in a box of its own and can be withdrawn at any time, by a removal issue or by email; the saves to the Internet Archive then stop without review, and what was done before stays lawful.
A person can also ask to receive the personal data they gave in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable form (Article 20); `papers.json` and the OAI-PMH interface already give every record in that form.
A person can object to the use of their personal data, as set out under "The right to object" above, and can complain to the data protection authority of their country.
Sophaxis has not appointed a representative in the European Union or the United Kingdom (Article 27).
The operator has decided not to appoint one.
A representative would be a paid service, or a person in the European Union or the United Kingdom who takes on liability for Sophaxis, and Sophaxis is run unpaid within free services.
Should the view above on Article 3(2) be wrong, Sophaxis does not meet Article 27, because it has no representative there; the processing is regular, so the exception for occasional processing does not apply.
The operator reviews this decision when Sophaxis first lists a work by an author other than the operator, and whenever a data protection authority or a person in the European Union or the United Kingdom asks for a representative.
Each review and its outcome are recorded in the public repository.
A review weighs two ways forward: appointing a representative, or running Sophaxis through a legal entity.
A legal entity established in Japan would not by itself settle the question of a representative; only an establishment in the European Union or the United Kingdom would, and the General Data Protection Regulation would then apply to that establishment in full.
Whatever form Sophaxis takes, it charges nothing, to authors or to readers.
People there write to the operator directly, in English or Japanese, at the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547).
The operator answers them, and the data protection authorities, directly, in place of a representative.
A record of the processing is kept in the public repository, in `docs/records-of-processing.md`.

<!-- text: GDPR 3; UK GDPR 3; GDPR 17; UK GDPR 17; GDPR 49; UK GDPR 49; GDPR 20; GDPR 27 -->

## People in China

From 2026-11-22, Sophaxis does not offer its service to people in China either.
Article 53 of China's Personal Information Protection Law requires a processor abroad that offers products or services to people in China to set up an agency or designate a representative in China, and Sophaxis has none.
This depends only on where a person lives or stays, not on nationality, race, ethnic origin or any other personal characteristic.
The rights in "Your choices" are honoured all the same, as far as they apply.

<!-- text: PIPL 53 -->

## People in Thailand

From 2026-11-22, Sophaxis does not offer its service to people in Thailand either.
Section 37(5) of Thailand's Personal Data Protection Act requires a controller abroad that offers goods or services to people in Thailand to designate in writing a representative in Thailand, and Sophaxis has none.
Section 38 exempts a controller that engages in the profession or business of processing personal data without a large amount of it; Sophaxis is not a business, so the exemption is not relied on.
This depends only on where a person lives or stays, not on nationality, race, ethnic origin or any other personal characteristic.
The rights in "Your choices" are honoured all the same, as far as they apply.

<!-- text: Thailand PDPA 37; Thailand PDPA 38 -->

## People in the other places

From 2026-11-22, Sophaxis does not offer its service to people in the other places that the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) lists either.
Their laws require, or are reported to require, a representative there, the storage of personal data there, registration there, or conditions before personal data leaves the place, and Sophaxis meets none of these.
A place is listed as soon as such a duty is reported, and taken off only after its law has been read at its source.
Russia's Federal Law No. 152-FZ also reaches the data of Russian citizens who live elsewhere, when they consent to its processing (Article 1(1.1)); Sophaxis decides by where a person lives or stays and does not ask about citizenship, so this reach is not covered, and the operator reviews the decision if a Russian authority raises it.
From 2026-11-22, Sophaxis does not list work by an author under 18 who lives or stays in India.
From 2027-05-13, Rule 10 of India's Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 lets the data of a person under 18 be processed only with the verifiable consent of a parent, and Sophaxis does not verify that consent.
This depends only on where a person lives or stays, not on nationality, race, ethnic origin or any other personal characteristic.
The rights in "Your choices" are honoured all the same, as far as they apply.

<!-- text: Russia 152-FZ 1; India DPDP Rules 10 -->

## Changes to this policy

When this policy changes, the date at the top changes.
Earlier versions stay in the public repository.

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html

# Withdrawal Policy

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [撤回の規程（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

## Who can withdraw

Any one author of a listed work can withdraw it.
A work is listed only while every author agrees, so the listing ends when one author withdraws that agreement.

The request comes from the author's own GitHub account, as at submission.
The author's ORCID record must link to that account, and the ORCID iD must belong to an author of the work.
An automatic check confirms both and posts the result in the issue.

## How to ask

Open a withdrawal issue and give the Sophaxis id, your ORCID iD and a short reason.
The reason is shown on the record page, so it must not contain personal data.
The issue is public.

A request that cannot be made in public goes by email to the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547).
The operator then confirms the author through the ORCID record, as the check does in the issue.

## What happens

The operator aims to act within 7 days of a verified request.
The record page keeps its address, its title, its authors, its abstract and its versions, so that citations do not break.
A notice at the top gives the date of withdrawal and the reason.
The record stays in the lists, the search, the feed and `papers.json`, marked as withdrawn.
The PDF copies are taken off the site, and the record links to the repository only.
A withdrawn record takes no new versions.
Earlier copies stay in the history of the public repository and in the Internet Archive, and harvesters of the OAI-PMH interface keep what they took.

## Removal at an author's request

An author can ask, in the same issue, for the record to be removed instead of withdrawn.
The form asks which of the two the author wants.
The same check confirms that the account asking belongs to an author of the work.
A record that is already withdrawn can still be removed.
The operator removes the record by labelling the verified issue `upheld`, and aims to do so within 7 days.
Only the Sophaxis id then stays, as the section "What a removed record leaves" in the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html) sets out.
No reason is shown, and the withdrawal issue itself is emptied, closed and locked.

## An author's name

As the Creative Commons licences provide, an author can ask for their name to be taken off a record.
The operator does so as far as is reasonably practicable, and the record stays.

## The work in its repository

Withdrawal on Sophaxis does not touch the deposit.
Sophaxis cannot withdraw or delete a work at Zenodo, Figshare or any other repository; a request about the deposit goes to that repository.
If the repository withdraws or deletes the deposit, the weekly check finds that the DOI no longer resolves, and the operator withdraws the record with a note that says so.

## Withdrawal on publication

Some publishers ask authors to remove a preprint when the work is published.
Any one author can then withdraw the listing as above.
If the published version is recorded, the record page keeps the link to it, so that a reader who follows a citation of the preprint finds the published version.
The authors can report the published version before they ask for withdrawal; a withdrawn record takes no new report.

## Withdrawal and removal

Withdrawal is the authors' decision, and the record stays.
Removal is for legal reasons, such as copyright infringement or exposure of personal data, or at an author's request, and takes the title, the authors, the abstract and the PDF copy off the site.
It follows the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html

# Takedown Policy

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [削除の規程（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

The laws, licences and terms that this page cites are quoted at the end of each section that cites them.
Japanese statutes are quoted in full, as the e-Gov law API gives them. The other texts are quoted word for word from their official sources, as fetched on 2026-11-11, and are not translated.
A citation whose source could not be fetched is named there as not quoted, with the reason.

## When a record is removed

Records are not deleted.
Every Sophaxis id stays, even when its record is removed.
A record is removed in three cases.
The first is removal required by law, such as copyright infringement or exposure of personal data.
The second is when an author shows that they did not agree to the listing and the work cannot be withdrawn under the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html).
The third is when an author of the work asks for it in a withdrawal issue, as the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html) sets out.
A removed record leaves only what the section "What a removed record leaves" below lists.

## How to ask

To request removal for legal reasons, open a removal issue.
Do not include personal data in the issue.
Describe where the problem is, without repeating the material itself.
Say how you are concerned: as an author, as the rights holder, as the person whose data appears, or on their behalf.

Requests are welcome from any country, in English or Japanese.
A request may rest on the law of the requester's country, such as a copyright notice under the law of the United States or a request under the data protection law of the European Union.
The operator considers it under this policy and under Japanese law, and takes the material offline when either requires it.

The site is served by Vercel, and the repository and its issues are kept on GitHub, both in the United States.
A request can also go to GitHub, for example as a copyright notice under its own process, or to Vercel.
They decide under their own terms; the operator decides on Sophaxis under this policy, whatever they decide.
Where the operator removes material, it also asks GitHub to remove it from the repository history, as set out below.

A request that cannot be made in public goes by email to the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547).
That is the address for requests; the address in the OAI-PMH interface is for harvesters.
For personal data and other serious harm, the operator then takes the record page (its title, authors, abstract and PDF copy) offline while the request is reviewed; authors agree to this in the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html).

## What happens

The operator aims to answer each request within 7 days.
For personal data and other serious harm, the record page (its title, authors, abstract and PDF copy) is taken offline at once, before the decision, and OAI-PMH reports the record as deleted until it is put back.
A removal issue is acknowledged automatically, with the day by which the operator aims to answer.
When a removal issue reports exposure of personal data, the record page (its title, authors, abstract and PDF copy) is taken offline automatically, before the operator reads it.
The automatic steps decide nothing; the operator decides every request.
The authors are told in their submission issue and can respond.
A request about the requester's own personal data concerns that person, not the work, so the authors are not told of it.
Except where serious harm requires it at once, the operator removes material on a request only after asking the authors whether they agree; if they do not object within 7 days, the operator may remove it.
This notice-and-response procedure follows the approach of Japanese law on the liability of providers of online services: the person whose material is concerned hears of the request and can answer before a decision, except where serious harm requires the material to be taken offline at once.

If the request is upheld, the record is removed, as the next section sets out.
If the request is not upheld, the operator says why in the issue.
Material that was taken offline while the request was reviewed is put back.
The decision is posted in the issue, or sent by email to a person who asked by email, before the material goes back.
An author can answer a request at any time; if the answer shows that the request has no ground, the material is put back.

## What a removed record leaves

This section applies to every removed record, whatever the reason.
The removal is carried out by `tools/removal.js` in the public repository, after the operator's decision, and every step below is checked automatically before it is published.

On the site:

- When a record is removed, its page is replaced by a notice that says only that the record with that Sophaxis id was removed.
- The notice gives no reason and no other detail.
- The address keeps working, so that citations lead to the notice instead of to nothing.
- The title, the authors, the abstract and the PDF copy are removed from the site.
- The page asks search engines not to index it, and the record leaves every list, the search, the feed, `papers.json` and the sitemap. The statistics count it only among removed records.
- Earlier versions of the site that Vercel keeps are not open to the public.
- `robots.txt` asks the Internet Archive's crawlers not to collect the page or its PDF copies again.

In the records and the OAI-PMH interface:

- The record keeps only its Sophaxis id, the word "removed" and the day of removal. The day is kept because the OAI-PMH interface needs it.
- The OAI-PMH interface marks the record as deleted, with that day and no metadata, so that harvesters can remove it when they next visit.

In the issues:

- Every automatic comment about the record is deleted, and the issues that name it are emptied, closed and locked; the operator then deletes them.
- Deleting an issue also deletes its edit history.
- A removal request itself stays, with the decision on it. A withdrawal issue that asked for removal is emptied like the others.

Outside the site:

- The operator also asks GitHub to remove the material from the repository history.
- Until GitHub does so, earlier versions of the record stay in the history of the public repository.
- GitHub's own procedure is to rewrite the history first and then ask GitHub Support, which helps only with sensitive data whose risk cannot be removed otherwise; where it does not help, the earlier versions stay in the history.
- The operator also asks the Internet Archive to exclude its earlier copies of the record.
- Copies that others have already taken are outside Sophaxis's control; the operator tells the ones it knows of.
- A follow-up issue lists these steps, with the request to the Internet Archive. Each day an automatic step checks whether the emptied issues are deleted and whether the Wayback Machine still lists a copy, ticks what is done, and reminds the operator once a week of the rest.

The Sophaxis id of a removed record is never given to another work.

## For the European Union: the Digital Services Act

From 2026-11-22, Sophaxis does not list work by an author who lives in the European Union, or who stays there between the submission and the listing, and does not direct itself to people there, so the operator considers that it has no substantial connection to the Union and does not offer services there in the sense of the Act.
Sophaxis takes the worst case here too, and follows the Digital Services Act of the European Union as far as it can apply to a service of its size.

- Point of contact, for authorities, the European Commission and people who use Sophaxis (Articles 11 and 12): the email address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547), in English or Japanese. Sophaxis has no legal representative in the European Union (Article 13), and the operator has decided not to appoint one, for the reason the [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html) gives. Authorities write to the operator directly at that address. Should the view above be wrong, Sophaxis does not meet Article 13, because it has no legal representative in the European Union.
- Notices of illegal content (Article 16): a removal issue, or an email. A notice by email names who sends it and gives an email address. A removal issue does not, because it is public; the GitHub account that opens it stands in their place. A notice by email also says that the sender believes in good faith that what it says is accurate and complete. A removal issue is acknowledged automatically; a notice by email is acknowledged by the operator by email, without undue delay. The decision is told in the issue or by email.
- Reasons for a decision (Article 17): the operator gives the grounds of every decision in the removal issue, or by email. The authors were pointed to that issue when the request arrived. The grounds say whether an automatic step acted: only the step that takes exposed personal data offline at once ever does, and it acts on the kind of problem that the request names. Where material is held to be illegal, the grounds name the law relied on and say why the material breaks it. They also say how far the measure reaches and for how long: a removal applies wherever the site is read, and it is permanent. When a request came by email and is upheld, the grounds, without personal data, are posted in the authors' submission issue before it is emptied, so that GitHub sends them to the authors who follow it; the removal cannot be run without them. An author can also ask the operator for them by email.
- Challenging a decision (Article 20): the person who sent the notice and the authors can challenge a decision within six months, by answering in the removal issue or by email. It costs nothing. The operator reviews it and answers, and the review is never left to an automatic step.
- A person can also go to a court, or to an out-of-court dispute settlement body certified under Article 21.
- Suspicions of serious crime (Article 18): if the operator learns of information that gives rise to a suspicion of a criminal offence that threatens a person's life or safety, the operator promptly tells the law enforcement or judicial authorities of the Member State concerned, with all relevant information it has. Where that Member State cannot be identified with reasonable certainty, the operator tells Europol.
- The rules that limit what may be listed are in the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html) and these policies, in plain English (Article 14).
- Average monthly active recipients (Article 24(3)): Sophaxis keeps no analytics and no identifiers of readers, and will not start keeping them to produce this figure. On request of a Digital Services Coordinator or the Commission, the operator gives, for each of the last six months, the number of people in the Union who submitted, reported or wrote to Sophaxis, counted from the issues and the email, and says that readers are not counted.
- The [statistics](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/stats.html) count the removed records and link to every public removal request.

<!-- text: DSA 11; DSA 12; DSA 13; DSA 16; DSA 17; DSA 20; DSA 21; DSA 18; DSA 14; DSA 24 -->

## Copyright notices under United States law

Sophaxis has not designated an agent with the United States Copyright Office, which charges a fee, so it does not rely on the limitation of liability in 17 U.S.C. 512.
A notice of claimed infringement under that law is handled under this policy, like any other request.

<!-- text: 17 U.S.C. 512 -->

## Requests to disclose who sent material

A request to disclose who submitted material is handled as Japanese law provides.
The operator first asks the person concerned for their opinion.
The operator discloses nothing that the law does not require.

## The work in its repository

Sophaxis cannot remove a work from Zenodo, Figshare or any other repository.
A request about the deposit itself goes to that repository.

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policy.html

# Policies

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [規程（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policy.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

Sophaxis is an overlay preprint server for philosophy and mathematics.
It lists preprints that authors have already deposited in an open repository,
and it gives each one a stable record page.

## What Sophaxis is not

Acceptance is moderation, not peer review.
A listing on Sophaxis says that a submission passed the checks in the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html).
It does not say that the work is correct, original or important.
Sophaxis does not guarantee the quality of any listed work.

Sophaxis is not a journal.
It does not assign DOIs.
The DOI stays with the repository where the author deposited the work, and it is the reference to cite.

## No fees

Sophaxis charges nothing, to authors or to readers.
There are no submission fees, no listing fees and no paid tiers.
It will not start charging.
It takes no donations, sponsorship or advertising.

## Commitments are never dropped silently

A commitment in these policies is never dropped silently.
The public repository keeps the list of commitments in `verification/commitments.txt`.
The automatic check fails if one disappears from the policies or from the list, unless the text that replaces it is named in `verification/superseded.txt`.
A change to a commitment that adds a duty for readers or authors is still announced in advance, as the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html) set out.

## Editorial independence

The moderator decides on each submission under the published policies, and on nothing else.
No repository, funder, institution, author or service can direct a decision.
No listing is given in return for money, a favour or a citation.
The reasons for every decision are public in its issue.

## Operator and conflicts of interest

Sophaxis is operated by Takuya Nemoto, in Japan.
The [Operator and contact](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.html) page says how to reach the operator.
Submissions by the operator are moderated under the same rules
and are marked on their record pages as the operator's own.

## Finding work

Each record can be listed in more than one field.
Authors with an ORCID iD have a page that lists their work on Sophaxis.
Authors without one have no such page, because a name alone can belong to several people.
New records are announced in an Atom feed, `feed.xml`.
The public part of every record is available as `papers.json`, for reuse.
Abstracts in both keep the licence of their work.

## About these pages

These pages describe how Sophaxis works and what it promises.
They are not legal advice.
Each policy is put in a few sentences on [The policies in brief](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/rules.html); the policies themselves govern.
Each page shows the date of its last change, and every earlier version is kept in the public repository.
The changes to the policies alone are also given, newest first, in an Atom feed of their own, apart from the news: [policies/changes.xml](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/changes.xml).
How the criteria for listing are reviewed and changed is said in the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html#changes-to-the-criteria).
Every policy, the Disclaimer and the pages that explain Sophaxis, such as this one, the FAQ and the Glossary, have Japanese translations, which the [Japanese top page](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/index.ja.html) lists, and the page on personal data has a Japanese version under the headings of Japan's Act; each is linked from the top of its English page. Where a translation differs from the English text, the English text applies.

This site and its code were built with Claude Code (Anthropic).
The operator is responsible for them. Claude is not an author.

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.html

# Disclaimer

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [免責事項（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

This page gathers in one place what Sophaxis does not promise.
The [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html) are binding; where this page differs, they apply.

## Listed work

Listing is moderation, not peer review.
Sophaxis does not check proofs, arguments or data, and does not guarantee that any listed work is correct, original, complete or of any quality.
The authors bear full responsibility for their work, including its statement on generative models, which Sophaxis does not verify.

## Metadata

Titles, authors, abstracts, licences, versions and dates come from the DOI metadata held by DataCite, Crossref and JaLC, and are shown as received; an abstract that the metadata does not have comes from the submission form.
An error there can appear here.
Errors can be reported through the link on each record page.

## The identity check

The automatic check confirms that the person who controls an ORCID record opened the submission issue, and that the ORCID iD belongs to an author of the work.
It is not an official identity check.

## No affiliation

Sophaxis is an independent, personal project.
It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or a partner of any repository it lists, nor of DataCite, Crossref, JaLC, OpenAlex, ORCID, GitHub, Vercel or the Internet Archive.
Their names are used only to identify their services, and belong to their owners. Some of them are trade marks.
They are not responsible for Sophaxis, for its records, or for any error that Sophaxis introduces; see the page [for repositories and DOI registration agencies](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/repositories.html).

## Who runs Sophaxis, and why

The operator, who is at present also the only moderator, runs Sophaxis as an unpaid volunteer.
No one is paid for work on Sophaxis, and no one pays to submit or to read.
Sophaxis is served only within the free services of GitHub and Vercel, at the address sophaxis.vercel.app, and has no domain or hosting to pay for.
The operator pays personally for Claude Code, the tool with which the site and its code are written (see How Sophaxis was made below).
Sophaxis takes no money from anyone to cover it.
Serving unpaid does not lessen what the operator owes readers and authors under the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html) and the [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html).

Sophaxis began because the operator looked for one place that lists open preprints in philosophy and in mathematics side by side, and did not find one.
It is kept for the operator's own reading, as the next section says, and for anyone who works on the same questions.
This is the operator's reason, not a judgement on other archives.
Sophaxis does not replace them, and a work listed here stays in its own repository.

## The operator's own use

The operator keeps Sophaxis as a hobby, as an extension of a personal reading shelf: a place to keep works in philosophy and mathematics at hand and to read them.
This use does not change what is listed or how.

- Only an author of a work can submit it. The operator does not list a work by someone else because the operator has read it or wants to keep it; such a work stays on the operator's own shelf, outside Sophaxis.
- Sophaxis is not run for profit. It charges no one, sells nothing, shows no advertising and earns nothing.
- Sophaxis does not publish works. Each work is published by its repository under its DOI, and Sophaxis links to it.
- A PDF copy is the unmodified file the authors deposited, shared only as the work's licence allows, with its authors, its licence and a link to the original; see the [Copyright Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/copyright.html).
- Sophaxis takes no copyright and no exclusive licence in any work.
- A rights holder can ask for the removal of a work under the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).

These choices keep Sophaxis within what the authors and the licences allow.
They are not legal advice, and they do not claim that no legal question can arise.

## GitHub and other services

Sophaxis runs on GitHub: its code, its records and its submissions (GitHub issues) are kept there, and its automatic checks run as GitHub Actions in the public repository.
The site is built from that repository and served by Vercel.
Sophaxis does not use GitHub or ORCID sign-in and asks no one for access to their accounts; it reads only public data, through the public APIs of DataCite, Crossref, JaLC, OpenAlex, ORCID and the repositories.
Using GitHub to submit is subject to GitHub's own terms and privacy statement.
GitHub and Vercel each provide their services "as is", without warranty, and limit their liability under their own terms; Sophaxis cannot promise more about their services than they do.
The site is served on Vercel's free Hobby plan, on which Vercel may disable or remove a deployment with or without notice. What their terms provide is set out in the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html), under "GitHub and Vercel".

## How Sophaxis was made

The site, its code, its policies and these pages were written with Claude Code, a coding tool by Anthropic, at the operator's request.
The operator reviewed them and is responsible for them; Claude is not an author of Sophaxis or of any listed work.
No language model decides on a submission: the automatic check is ordinary code, and every decision is made by a moderator.
Sophaxis is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.
Claude Code is named as a disclosure of how the site was made, not as an endorsement or an advertisement.
The operator is an ordinary paying user of it.
Sophaxis has no arrangement with Anthropic, receives nothing from it, and does not link to its products.

## Links

Sophaxis links to repositories, DOIs and other sites that it does not control.
It is not responsible for their content, their availability or their terms.

## Availability

The site is provided as it is, and may be unavailable, change or close.
If it closes, the repository with every record stays public; see Continuity in the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html).

Sophaxis depends on outside services:

- If Vercel stops, the site is not served; the records stay in the repository on GitHub and in the Internet Archive.
- If GitHub stops, no one can submit, and the automatic checks do not run; the site keeps showing what it last built.
- If DataCite, Crossref or JaLC cannot be reached, a submission cannot be checked until they can.
- If a repository removes a deposit, its DOI stops resolving, and the record is withdrawn under the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html).

## Not advice

The policies and pages of Sophaxis describe how Sophaxis works.
They are not legal or professional advice.

## Liability

The operator is liable, as Japanese law provides, for loss that the operator causes by intent or negligence.
The operator is not liable for loss caused only by the content of a listed work, which its authors write, or only by GitHub, Vercel or a repository, unless the law makes the operator liable for it.
Sophaxis applies Japan's Consumer Contract Act to readers and authors as if its operator were a business operator under it.
This does not exclude or limit liability for intent or gross negligence, or any liability that the law does not allow to be excluded or limited.
The responsibility for an act done by someone else against the Terms of Use, or outside them, lies with the person who did it.
Except where the law makes the operator responsible, the operator is not responsible for such acts. The Terms of Use list such acts that may come near a law, under "Acts outside these rules that may come near a law".
These terms are governed by the laws of Japan, and nothing on this page limits a right that the law does not allow to be limited.
Disputes are settled by agreement first, as the section Disputes in the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html) sets out.
