# Frequently asked questions

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [よくある質問（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/faq.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

Each answer is a short form of a policy. Where they differ, the policy applies.

A question is added here only when someone has actually asked it, in an issue or by email.
Its answer then begins with a line that says when and where it was asked, such as "Asked on 2026-12-01, in issue #300." or "Asked on 2026-12-01, by email.", without the name of the person who asked.
The questions without such a line were already here on 2026-11-11, when this rule began; they were written from the policies.

## What is Sophaxis?

An overlay preprint server for philosophy, mathematics, logic, the philosophy of mathematics and the philosophy of science.
The work itself is published by its repository; Sophaxis keeps an unmodified PDF copy only where the licence allows.
It lists preprints that authors have already deposited in an open repository, and gives each one a stable record page.

## Is it peer review?

No. Acceptance is moderation, not peer review.
Moderation checks the submitter, the licence, the scope, the form of the paper and the statement on generative models.
It does not check proofs, arguments or data, and Sophaxis does not guarantee the quality of any listed work.
See the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html).

## Does it cost anything?

No. Sophaxis charges nothing, to authors or to readers, and will not start charging.

## Does Sophaxis give my work a DOI?

No. The DOI comes from the repository where you deposited the work, and it is the reference to cite.
Sophaxis gives each record an id, such as 2026.0001, which never changes and is never reused.

## Which repositories are accepted?

Zenodo, Figshare, OSF Preprints, SocArXiv, MetaArXiv, arXiv, Preprints.org, SSRN, Research Square, SciELO Preprints, Qeios, ScienceOpen Preprints, Advance, KC Works and Jxiv.
The work must have a DOI from one of them.

## Which licences are accepted?

CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 and CC0 1.0, as given in the DOI metadata.
Licences with NonCommercial or NoDerivatives terms are not accepted, and neither is the arXiv non-exclusive licence.
See the [Licence Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/licences.html).

## Who can submit?

Only an author of the work, with an ORCID iD.
Your ORCID record must link to your GitHub account, and an automatic check confirms that your ORCID iD belongs to an author of the work.
Every author must agree to the listing.
See the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html).

## Why GitHub?

Submissions are GitHub issues.
This keeps every step public and lets the automatic check confirm that the account opening the issue belongs to an author.
Sophaxis has no accounts of its own and no passwords.

## Is Sophaxis connected to GitHub and ORCID?

Yes, in public only.
The code, the records and the submissions are on GitHub, and the automatic checks run as GitHub Actions in the public repository.
ORCID is read through its public API.
Sophaxis does not use GitHub or ORCID sign-in, asks no one for access to their accounts, and is not affiliated with either; see the [Disclaimer](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.html).

## Was Sophaxis made with a language model?

Yes. The site, its code and its policies were written with Claude Code (Anthropic) at the operator's request.
The operator is responsible for them, and Claude is not an author.
No language model decides on a submission.
See the [Disclaimer](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.html).

## Can I use language models?

Yes, if you disclose how.
Name the tools and say what they were used for; this covers every generative model, including those that make images or code.
A generative model cannot be an author.
The statement is shown on the record page.

## How long does moderation take?

As a guide, a decision can come on the day of submission, but it can also take several weeks or a few months.
A slow decision does not mean that submissions are paused; when they are, the top page says so.
[From submission to listing](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/process.html) follows a submission step by step.

## Who is responsible for a listed work?

The authors bear full responsibility for the work and its listing: its content, the rights to share it, material from others, personal data in it and the statement on generative models.
See the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html).

## How do I add a new version?

Deposit it in the repository, then submit it as an update and give the existing Sophaxis id.
Earlier versions stay listed.

## My work has been published in a journal. Can I submit it?

Only a version that you may share under an accepted licence.
Give the DOI of the published version in the form, and the record shows it.

## My listed preprint has been published. What do I do?

Report it with the [published-version form](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=published.yml), as one of its authors.
The preprint stays listed, and its record page shows the published version at the top and asks readers to cite it.
Sophaxis does not judge peer review: the record repeats what you state about it.
The details are in the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html), under "When the work is published".

## Does Sophaxis keep a copy of the PDF?

Where the repository allows a script to fetch it, Sophaxis keeps an unmodified copy, so that search engines can index the full text.
For any other repository, you can attach the deposited PDF to your submission issue.
A copy is kept only if the file is at most 20 MB.
See the [Copyright Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/copyright.html).

## Will my work appear in Google Scholar?

Each record page carries the tags that Google Scholar reads, and the sitemap lists every page.
Scholar takes a PDF only from the directory of its record page, so each PDF copy is also served there.
When a record page or a PDF copy is new, changed or removed, the search engines that take IndexNow, such as Bing, are told as soon as it is live. A new or changed page is also saved to the Internet Archive, where every author of the work consents to it. Google reads the sitemap instead.
Sophaxis cannot promise that a search engine will index a page.

## What should I check before submitting?

The [checklist](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/checklist.html) gathers what the policies ask, with examples of a statement on generative models.
It also offers two paper templates, in Markdown and in LaTeX, under CC0 1.0. Using them is not required.

## Does Sophaxis track readers?

No. The site sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads nothing from other servers, as the [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html) says.
It shows no counts of views or downloads.

## Is there a mailing list?

No. Sophaxis sends no newsletter and collects no email addresses for one.
New records and news can be followed through the Atom feeds: [new preprints](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/feed.xml), [news](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/news.xml), and one feed for each field.

## How do I cite a work listed here?

Cite the DOI of the version you read.
Each record page gives the citation in APA, Chicago and BibTeX, and as BibTeX, RIS and CSL-JSON files.

## How do I report an error in a record?

Use the link "Report an error in this record" on its page.
Corrections are added to the record as dated notes.

## Can I withdraw my work?

Yes. Any one author can withdraw a listed work.
The record page stays with a withdrawal notice, so that citations do not break, and the PDF copies are taken off the site.
See the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html).

## How do I ask for material to be removed?

For copyright infringement, exposure of personal data or another legal reason, follow the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html).

## What happens to the records if Sophaxis closes?

The repository with every record stays public, so that the records stay readable.
Each week, Sophaxis also asks the Internet Archive to save its pages and the PDF copies, where every author of the work consents to it.

## Who runs Sophaxis, and how do I reach the operator?

See the [Operator and contact](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.html) page.

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/process.html

# From submission to listing

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [投稿から掲載まで（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/process.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

This page follows one submission from start to finish.
The rules themselves are in the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) and the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html); where this page differs, they apply.

## Before you start

You need four things. The [checklist](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/checklist.html) gathers the rest of what a submission needs.

1. A preprint deposited in Zenodo, Figshare, OSF Preprints, SocArXiv, MetaArXiv, arXiv, Preprints.org, SSRN, Research Square, SciELO Preprints, Qeios, ScienceOpen Preprints, Advance, KC Works or Jxiv, with a DOI. From 2026-11-23, at least six months must have passed since the first DOI of the work was registered, as the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) sets out.
2. CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 1.0 on the deposit, so that it appears in the DOI metadata.
3. An [ORCID](https://orcid.org) iD. Registration is free.
4. A [GitHub](https://github.com) account. Registration is free.

Every author of the work must agree to the listing.
From 2026-11-23, a first submission also needs a researcher to vouch for it, with a journal article, a book chapter or a book, as the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) sets out.
If you used language models or other generative models, note which tools you used and what for.
From 2026-11-24, the form also asks for statements on funding, on competing interests, and on human participants and research ethics, and, as an option, where the data and code are.

## Step 1. Find your GitHub username

A submission is a GitHub issue: a public post in the Sophaxis repository, with comments below it.
If you have no GitHub account, create one at [github.com/signup](https://github.com/signup).

Your username is the last part of the address of your GitHub profile, `https://github.com/<your username>`.
After you sign in, it also appears in the menu under your picture at the top right.

## Step 2. Link your ORCID record to GitHub

1. Sign in at [orcid.org](https://orcid.org). Your ORCID record opens; your ORCID iD is the 16-digit number under your name.
2. Find the section "Websites & social links" and click its edit button (the pencil).
3. Choose "Add link". Give a title, such as GitHub, and the address `https://github.com/<your username>`.
4. Set its visibility to "Everyone", then save.

This is how Sophaxis confirms that the person who opens the submission is an author of the work.
Sophaxis reads only the name, the links and the works in your ORCID record; it never asks ORCID for your email address or your country.

## Step 3. Open a submission issue

1. Open the [submission form](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=submission.yml). If GitHub asks you to sign in, do so; the form then opens. The same form is also [in Japanese](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=submission-ja.yml).
2. After "[Submission]" in the title, add a few words, such as the title of your work.
3. Give the DOI, your ORCID iD, the category (and a subfield, if one fits), the statement on generative models and, from 2026-11-24, the statements on funding, competing interests and research ethics, and tick the confirmations. A summary in plain words and an abstract in a second language are optional.
4. Press the button at the bottom of the form to create the issue.

The title, the authors, the abstract and the licence are taken from the DOI metadata; you do not type them.

The issue is public.
Your GitHub username and everything you write in it can be read by anyone.
GitHub tells you about each new comment on an issue you opened, on github.com and, by default, by email.

## Step 4. The automatic check answers

Usually within a few minutes, a comment titled "Automatic checks" appears in the issue.
It shows each check as pass or fail: the repository, the licence, the DOI metadata, the link from your ORCID record and your authorship.
The issue receives the label `verified` or `unverified`.

If a check fails, the comment says why.
Fix the cause, for example the link in your ORCID record, then edit the issue; the check runs again.
To edit the issue, open the menu (⋯) at the top right of your first post, choose "Edit", change what is needed and save.
An edit that changes nothing does not start the check.

If the repository does not let Sophaxis fetch the PDF (every repository except Zenodo, Figshare, arXiv and Research Square), the comment asks you to attach the deposited PDF to the issue.
This is optional, and the file must be at most 20 MB.
To attach it, drag the file into the comment box at the bottom of the issue, wait until its link appears, and post the comment.

When the submission is verified, the comment may also give advice on the DOI metadata at the repository, for example a missing abstract, licence or keywords.
The advice comes from [deposit-check](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/deposit-check). It does not decide the listing.
Search engines and indexes read this metadata rather than the PDF, and most repositories let you correct it without making a new version.

A pass is not acceptance.

The buttons on GitHub and ORCID may be renamed over time; the steps stay the same.

## Step 5. A moderator reads the submission

A moderator reads the verified submission against the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html):
the scope, the form of a scholarly paper, the statement on generative models, and the absence of spam, abuse and personal data of third parties.
Moderation is not peer review. It does not check proofs, arguments or data.

As a guide, a decision can come on the day of submission, but it can also take several weeks or a few months.
The decision is written in the issue.

## Step 6. The decision

If the submission is accepted, its record page is published with a Sophaxis id, such as 2026.0001, and the issue is closed.
Where the repository allows, an unmodified copy of the PDF is added afterwards.

If it is declined, the moderator gives a short reason in the issue.
You can answer there.
The operator then looks at the submission once more, and that decision is final.

## After listing

- A new version: deposit it in the repository, then open a submission issue that gives the existing Sophaxis id.
- An error in the record: use "Report an error in this record" on its page.
- Withdrawal: any one author can withdraw the work under the [Withdrawal Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/withdrawal.html).
- Publication: when a later version is published in a journal, in proceedings or in a book, any one author reports it with the [published-version form](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=published.yml). The preprint stays listed.

Short answers to other questions are in the [FAQ](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/faq.html).

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/automation.html

# What runs by itself

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [自動で動く手順（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/automation.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

Sophaxis runs a number of steps by itself, as GitHub Actions in its public repository and as deployments on Vercel.
This page lists every one of them: when it runs, what it reads, what it writes, and what it leaves to the operator.
The code of each step is public, and each section links to it.

- No automatic step decides on a submission, a withdrawal, a correction or a removal request. The operator decides every one.
- One step acts before the operator decides: when a removal issue reports exposure of personal data, the record page (its title, authors, abstract and PDF copy) is taken offline at once. This protects the person concerned, is not a decision on the request, and is undone if the request is not upheld.
- No step uses a language model. The steps are ordinary code.
- No step signs in to any account. The only key is the token that GitHub gives each run, with the least permissions the step needs; the IndexNow key is public by design.
- A step that changes the records builds the site and runs every check first, and changes nothing if a check fails.
- The [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html) says what personal data these steps handle.

## When a submission issue is opened or edited, or an author confirms in a comment

- Reads: the DOI metadata from DataCite, Crossref or JaLC; the day each DOI that the metadata names as an earlier version of the work was registered; the notices that Crossref records against the DOI; the PDF of the latest version, where the repository lets a script fetch it, only to read its shape for the moderator, deleted after the reading; the day the issue was opened; the name, the websites and the works of the public ORCID record given in the form; advice on the metadata from deposit-check.
- Writes: a comment with the result of each check and a draft record, and the label `verified` or `unverified`.
- It checks that every required box of the form is ticked, reading the boxes from the two submission forms in the repository: the confirmations always, the consent and agreement from 2026-11-21, and where the authors live from 2026-11-22. The [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html#what-the-submitter-confirms) lists the same boxes.
- From 2026-11-21, it also counts each other author's confirmation, as the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) sets out.
- From 2026-11-23, it also checks that six months have passed since the first DOI of the work was registered, counted to the day the issue was opened, as the Submission Policy sets out.
- From 2026-11-23, it also checks that Crossref records no retraction, withdrawal or removal for the DOI, and sends an expression of concern to the operator.
- From 2026-11-24, it also checks that the statements on funding, on competing interests, and on human participants and research ethics are given. It does not judge what they say.
- From 2026-11-23, for a submitter who is not yet an author of a listed work, it also counts a researcher who vouches for the work: it reads the name, the websites and the works of that researcher's public ORCID record, and runs again when such a comment is written, edited or deleted.
- Leaves to the operator: accepting or declining the submission.
- Code: [tools/intake.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/intake.js), run by [intake.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/intake.yml).

## When a withdrawal issue is opened or edited

- Reads: the record, and the public ORCID record given in the form.
- Writes: a comment with the result of each check and, for a withdrawal, the record as it would be after it; the label `verified` or `unverified`.
- Leaves to the operator: withdrawing the record by a pull request, or removing it by labelling the verified issue `upheld`.
- Code: [tools/withdraw.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/withdraw.js).

## When a published version is reported

- Reads: the record, the DOI metadata of the published version, and the public ORCID record given in the form.
- Writes: a comment with the result of each check and the record with its published version.
- Leaves to the operator: recording the published version.
- Code: [tools/published.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/published.js).

## When a removal issue is opened or edited

- Reads: the record and the issues of the repository.
- Writes: an acknowledgement with the day by which the operator aims to answer, and a notice to the authors in their submission issue.
- When the issue reports exposure of personal data, it also takes the record page (its title, authors, abstract and PDF copy) offline at once, as the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html) says.
- Leaves to the operator: the decision.
- Code: [tools/removal.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/removal.js), run by [removal.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/removal.yml).

## When the operator labels a request `upheld` or `not-upheld`

- Acts only on the label of the repository owner.
- Upheld: removes the record, as "What a removed record leaves" in the Takedown Policy sets out, deletes the automatic comments about it, and empties, closes and locks the issues that name it.
- Not upheld: puts back what was taken offline, from the git history.
- After a removal, opens a follow-up issue that lists what is left by hand: deleting the emptied issues, a request to the Internet Archive with its draft, and GitHub's procedure for the repository history.
- Leaves to the operator: the grounds of the decision, deleting the emptied issues, and sending the requests to GitHub and the Internet Archive.
- A request sent by email is handled the same way: the operator runs the step by hand with the Sophaxis id and, for a decision, the grounds, which are posted in the authors' submission issue before it is emptied.

## Once a day, at 09:17 Japan time

- Reads: the open removal requests and the verified withdrawals.
- Writes: one reminder in each that the operator has not answered, from two days before the 7 days run out.
- Follow-ups of removals: ticks the deleted issues once GitHub answers that they are gone, and the request to the Internet Archive once the Wayback Machine lists no capture of the record page or its PDF copies. Closes the follow-up when everything is ticked, and reminds once a week of what is not.

## Once a month, on the 1st at 09:17 Japan time

- Reads: the records and `data/news.json`.
- Writes: an issue with a post in English and one in Japanese for the official account on X, each within the 280 characters that X counts, naming what was listed and announced in the month before. A month with nothing new gets no issue.
- Leaves to the operator: posting it. X's API is paid, so nothing is posted to X automatically.
- Also measures whether Sophaxis still fits its free services: the deployments on the busiest day of the last 30 days against the 100 a day of Vercel's free plan, the PDF copies against the limits in `site.json`, and the repository against the 1 GB that GitHub recommends. It writes the table to the run's summary, and opens an issue only when a measure reaches 80 percent. Vercel's bandwidth and function use are not measured; only the operator's Vercel account shows them.
- Code: [tools/monthly.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/monthly.js) and [tools/limits.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/limits.js), run by [monthly.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/monthly.yml).

## Once a year, on 2 January at 12:23 Japan time

- Reads: the public issues labelled submission, withdrawal or removal, the comments of the repository owner on declined submissions, and the records.
- Writes: an issue with the counts of the year before: submissions opened, accepted, declined and not decided yet, the reasons named for declining, the days from submission to a decision, the requests, and the records withdrawn and removed.
- Leaves to the operator: recording the counts in `data/reports/`, from which the [Decisions by year](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/decisions.html) page is built.
- Code: [tools/report.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/report.js) and [tools/report_issue.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/report_issue.js), run by [report.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/report.yml).

## Once a year, on 30 October at 09:17 Japan time

- Reads: the section "Yearly audit" of [docs/operations.md](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/docs/operations.md), the operator's routine.
- Writes: an issue on the day Sophaxis began, with that list to tick, unless an issue of the same title exists.
- Leaves to the operator: the audit itself.
- Code: [tools/audit.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/audit.js), run by [audit.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/audit.yml).

## On every push and every pull request, and once a week

- Runs every check of [verification/check.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/verification/check.js) against the records, the policies and the built site.
- Among them, a scan of every file in the repository for keys, tokens and email addresses other than the few the checks allow.
- The same checks also run on main once a week, on Monday at 14:07 Japan time, so that a check that depends on the date, and the scan, run even when nothing is pushed. A failure is shown in the repository's Actions, and the operator is told by GitHub.
- The operator merges a change only when the checks pass.

## When the site changes

- Vercel serves the files that the repository holds in `site/`, which `build.js` builds from the records. The OAI-PMH interface is a small function on Vercel that reads the same records.
- Once the new pages are live, the search engines that take IndexNow are told which record pages and PDF copies are new, changed or gone, and the new and changed ones are saved to the Internet Archive, if their authors consented to it. A gone page is never saved.
- Earlier versions of the site that Vercel keeps are not open to the public.
- After every push to main, and once a day at 11:41 Japan time, every file in `site/` is fetched from the live site and compared byte for byte with main. A difference that remains after ten minutes (a deployment that failed, or that the daily limit of the free plan refused) opens an issue, which closes by itself when the site matches.
- Code: [tools/live.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/live.js), run by [live.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/live.yml).
- `robots.txt` is built with the rest of the site, and asks the Internet Archive's crawlers not to collect any removed record, or any record whose authors did not consent to the saves.
- Code: [tools/indexnow.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/indexnow.js), run by [indexnow.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/indexnow.yml) and after each push of the removal step.

## Once a week, on Monday at 13:37 Japan time

- Reads: the DOI metadata of every listed version, the notices that Crossref records against each of them, the metadata of published versions, and how OpenAlex holds each work. In a workflow of its own at the same time, the articles of Japanese law and the GitHub terms that the [legal review](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/docs/legal-review.md) relies on, from the e-Gov law API and GitHub, and the privacy statements of Vercel and Apple, from their sites.
- Writes: an issue when a DOI stops resolving, a licence changes, Crossref records a notice that the record does not hold, a new version appears or a published version may exist; a pull request when an article of law, a GitHub term, or the date of the last update of Vercel's or Apple's privacy statement differs from the value recorded in `verification/statutes.json`, with the new values and texts and, for an article, the difference of its sentences (where the repository does not let workflows open pull requests, an issue with a link that opens it); an issue when one of them cannot be read; a summary of the run; a save to the Internet Archive of every page and PDF copy whose authors consented to it.
- Leaves to the operator: acting on what the issue reports, and reading the difference before recording it.
- Code: [tools/watch.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/watch.js), run by [watch.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/watch.yml), and [tools/statutes.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/statutes.js), run by [statutes.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/statutes.yml), which on a pull request only prints.

## When the operator labels the watch's pull request `record`

- Acts only on the label of the repository owner, and only on the branch `statutes/record`, which may change only `verification/statutes.json`, `verification/statutes-texts.json` and the changelog.
- Merges it into main, fills in the changelog's pull request number, runs every check and the watch itself on the merged result, and pushes only if all pass. The merge names the workflow as co-author.
- Leaves to the operator: reading the difference, and changing the policies first if the change requires it.
- Code: [tools/record.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/record.js), run by [record.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/record.yml).

## Only when the operator runs it

- Copies the PDF of a listed record from its repository onto a branch of its own, for a pull request that the operator reviews.
- Code: [tools/fetch_pdf.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/fetch_pdf.js).
- Fetches the texts of law, licences and terms that the legal pages cite, from their official sources, and writes the cited articles to `verification/sources-raw.json` on a new branch `sources/<date>`, never on main. The operator reads them before any quotation in `verification/sources.json` is taken from them.
- Code: [tools/sources.js](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/tools/sources.js), run by [sources.yml](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/blob/main/.github/workflows/sources.yml).

## What stays by hand

- Every decision, and its grounds.
- Deleting emptied issues, which the follow-up issue lists.
- Asking GitHub to remove material from the repository history, and the Internet Archive to exclude earlier copies, with the drafts in the follow-up issue.
- Recording a changed text of law or terms, by the label `record`.
- Registering Sophaxis with indexes and registries.
- Answering email.

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/transparency.html

# Transparency: a self-assessment

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [透明性の自己評価（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/transparency.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

COPE, DOAJ, OASPA and WAME publish the [Principles of Transparency and Best Practice in Scholarly Publishing](https://doaj.org/apply/transparency/).
This page holds Sophaxis against version 5.0 of October 2026, read at DOAJ on 2026-11-09, heading by heading.
It is the operator's own assessment, not one made or endorsed by any of the four organisations, and Sophaxis is not a member of any of them.

The Principles are written for journals.
Sophaxis is not a journal: it is an overlay preprint server, and acceptance is moderation, not peer review.
Where a principle cannot apply to a preprint server, this page says so, and does not count it as met.

Each heading gets one of four marks:

- **Met**: Sophaxis does what the principle asks, and the page says where.
- **In part**: Sophaxis does some of it; the page says what is missing.
- **Not met**: Sophaxis does not do it; the page says why.
- **Does not apply**: the principle is about something Sophaxis does not do.

## Summary

| Heading | Mark |
| --- | --- |
| Name | Met |
| Website | Met |
| Publishing schedule and timeline | Met |
| Preservation | In part |
| Copyright | In part |
| Licensing | Met |
| Publication ethics and related editorial policies | Met |
| Editorial assessment | Met |
| Peer review | Does not apply |
| Access | Met |
| Ownership and management | Met |
| Editorial board or advisory body | Not met |
| Editorial team and contact information | In part |
| Author fees | Met |
| Other revenue | Met |
| Advertising | Met |
| Direct marketing | Met |

## Journal presentation

### Name

Met.
The name Sophaxis says what the site is in its tagline, "Preprints in Philosophy and Mathematics", and the site says that it is not a journal ([Policies](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policy.html)) and has no affiliation with any repository or organisation ([Disclaimer](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.html)).

### Website

Met.
The site is served only over HTTPS, at one address, which is `https://sophaxis.vercel.app/` and no other.
The repository on GitHub points to it.
Its pages run no third-party script, set no cookie and use no analytics, under a strict Content Security Policy ([Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html)).
Sophaxis has no ISSN, so none is listed.

### Publishing schedule and timeline

Met.
Records are listed continuously, when a submission is accepted; there are no issues or volumes ([From submission to listing](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/process.html)).

### Preservation

In part.
The works themselves are deposited, and preserved, in their repositories, such as Zenodo, arXiv or Figshare.
The records and the site are kept in a public git repository, and version 1.0.0 is archived at Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.24033372).
Record pages and PDF copies are saved to the Internet Archive each week, where every author consents to it.
Sophaxis is in no archive of the Keepers Registry, such as CLOCKSS or Portico.

### Copyright

In part.
Authors keep their copyright; Sophaxis asks for no transfer and no exclusive licence ([Copyright Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/copyright.html)).
The site's own text is CC BY 4.0 and its code MIT, held by the operator.
The copyright holder printed on the full text is whatever the authors put in their PDF; Sophaxis keeps the file unmodified and does not add a statement.

### Licensing

Met.
Every listed work carries CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 1.0 in its DOI metadata, and its record page links the licence on the Creative Commons website ([Licence Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/licences.html)).
These licences let anyone mine the works, AI companies included, and `robots.txt` lets every crawler read the site; only the Internet Archive's crawlers are kept from removed records and from records whose authors did not consent to the saves.
The Terms of Use say how GitHub and Vercel may use public content, including to train AI models ([Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html)).

## Journal practices

### Publication ethics and related editorial policies

Met.
The statements on funding, competing interests and research ethics are asked from 2026-11-24, after the notice of 14 days that the Terms of Use give.

- Aims and scope: stated on the top page and in the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html). Met.
- Authorship, and the use of AI: only an author can submit, every author must agree, and the use of language models and other generative models must be disclosed, with its extent; a model cannot be an author. Met.
- Conflicts of interest: the operator's own submissions are marked, get no priority and wait seven days in public before listing ([Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html)). From 2026-11-24, the authors state their competing interests in the form, and the record page shows the statement ([Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html)). Met.
- Data sharing and reproducibility: the Submission Policy encourages authors to say where the data and code are, and the form asks it as an option; it is not required and not checked. Met.
- Funding and support: from 2026-11-24, the authors name every funder, with grant numbers, or say that there was none, and the record page shows the statement. Met.
- Post-publication review: anyone can report an error in a record by a public issue. Met.
- Corrections, retractions and expressions of concern: corrections are dated notes; the notices that Crossref records, including those from Retraction Watch, are read at submission and each week, and shown on the record. Met.
- Plagiarism: the Moderation Policy defines plagiarism, including the reuse of the authors' own work as new, and a submission found to plagiarise is declined; Sophaxis runs no software check. Met.
- Complaints and appeals: a declined submitter can answer in the issue, and the operator looks once more; requests to remove follow the [Takedown Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/takedown.html). Met.
- Research ethics: from 2026-11-24, every submission states whether it involves human participants, and one that does names the ethics approval, or why none was needed, and the consent of identifiable participants; work with personal data of third parties is declined. Met.
- Allegations of research misconduct: the Moderation Policy, under "Research integrity", says how a concern is raised, in public or by email, how the authors answer, that Sophaxis does not investigate and refers to the institution or journal, what a note on the record may say, and that a person who writes by email is not named. It follows the steps that COPE recommends, as far as one person can. Met.

### Editorial assessment

Met.
The operator, who is at present the only moderator, accepts or declines each submission in its public issue, on the reasons the Moderation Policy lists; no fee exists that could influence a decision.
Three language models, Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Grok (xAI), assist the review, given only public parts by hand, and decide nothing; the Moderation Policy says so.
No submission is guaranteed acceptance, and every record page says that acceptance is moderation, not peer review.
The [Decisions by year](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/decisions.html) page counts the decisions, with the reasons and the time to a decision.

### Peer review

Does not apply.
Sophaxis does not peer review.
Its moderation checks scope, form, licence, authorship and disclosure, as the Moderation Policy sets out, and the site says on every record that acceptance is moderation, not peer review.

### Access

Met.
Every page and every PDF copy is free to read, with no registration.

## Organisation

### Ownership and management

Met.
Sophaxis is owned and run by one person, named with an ORCID iD on the [Operator and contact](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.html) page, unpaid, within free services.
It has no affiliation with any society, institution or sponsor.

### Editorial board or advisory body

Not met.
Sophaxis has no editorial board and no advisory body.
The Moderation Policy says that other moderators may be invited, and names how; none has been invited yet.
Since 2026-11-10 a call for an advisory board has been open ([Advisory board: a call](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/advisory.html)); no adviser has joined yet.

### Editorial team and contact information

In part.
The operator's name and ORCID iD are on the contact page, and the email address is on the ORCID record.
No postal address is published: the operator is one private person.

## Business practices

### Author fees

Met.
Sophaxis charges nothing, to authors or to readers, and the Terms of Use say that no change will introduce fees.

### Other revenue

Met.
Sophaxis has no revenue: it is run unpaid within the free services of GitHub and Vercel, and the operator pays personally for Claude Code, with which it is written ([Disclaimer](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.html)).

### Advertising

Met.
Sophaxis shows no advertising, and declines a submission that advertises.

### Direct marketing

Met.
The site has no mailing list, asks no one for an email address, and sends no messages.

---

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/repositories.html

# For repositories and DOI registration agencies

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [預け先と DOI 登録機関へ（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/repositories.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

This page is addressed to the repositories whose deposits Sophaxis lists, and to the agencies that register their DOIs.
It says what Sophaxis reads from your services, how often, and what it does with it.

## The repositories listed

{{repositories}}

A work is listed only if its authors submit it, and only if its DOI metadata carries CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or CC0 1.0.
Sophaxis does not harvest or mirror any repository.

## What Sophaxis reads

- The DOI metadata of a submitted work, from the public REST APIs of DataCite, Crossref and, for Jxiv, JaLC: once when the work is submitted or its issue is edited, and once a week for each listed DOI, to confirm that it still resolves and keeps its licence.
- The list of versions of a work, from the same metadata.
- The PDF of a version, unmodified, only where the work's licence allows it and the repository offers it to scripts (Zenodo, Figshare, arXiv and Research Square), through their public APIs or download addresses. The copy is taken once per version, when the operator starts it by hand. The check of a submission, when its issue is opened or edited, also fetches the PDF of the latest version, only to read its shape for the moderator, and deletes it after the reading. Where the repository publishes a checksum, the copy must match it.

Every request that Sophaxis's own code makes names Sophaxis and its repository in its User-Agent: `Sophaxis (https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis)`. The advice step of the submission check runs [deposit-check](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/deposit-check), which names itself: `deposit-check (https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/deposit-check)`.
Sophaxis reads no pages meant for people, and does not get around any limit or block.

## What Sophaxis shows

Each record page links to the DOI and names the repository, and asks readers to cite the DOI.
The DOI stays the reference; Sophaxis gives no DOIs of its own.
The abstract and any PDF copy are shown under the work's own licence, with its authors, as the [Copyright Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/copyright.html) sets out.

## If something should change

If Sophaxis reads more often than you allow, reads something your terms do not allow, or should stop copying files from your service, tell the operator.
Sophaxis will change or stop it.
A request about a deposit itself stays with the repository; Sophaxis cannot change or remove a deposit.

Reach the operator through an [issue](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues) or by email to the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547).

## Disclaimer toward repositories and registration agencies

Sophaxis is independent, and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or a partner of any repository or registration agency.
Sophaxis keeps a community at Zenodo (<https://zenodo.org/communities/sophaxis>) for the Zenodo records of works it lists. Any Zenodo user can open one; it does not make Sophaxis part of Zenodo.
A record on Sophaxis is Sophaxis's own description of a deposit; it is not a statement by the repository or the agency.
They are not responsible for Sophaxis, for its records, for its moderation, or for any error that Sophaxis introduces when it shows their metadata.
Their names identify their services only, and their trademarks belong to them; Sophaxis shows none of their logos.
Sophaxis uses each service through its public interfaces and within its published terms, as Sophaxis understands them; where a service says otherwise, Sophaxis follows the service.
See also the [Disclaimer](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.html).

## Acknowledgements

Sophaxis exists because these services make research and its metadata openly available. Sophaxis thanks:

{{acknowledgements}}

Thank you to arXiv for use of its open access interoperability.

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.html

# Operator and contact

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [運営者と連絡先（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

The laws, licences and terms that this page cites are quoted at the end of each section that cites them.
Japanese statutes are quoted in full, as the e-Gov law API gives them. The other texts are quoted word for word from their official sources, as fetched on 2026-11-11, and are not translated.
A citation whose source could not be fetched is named there as not quoted, with the reason.

## Operator

Sophaxis is operated by one person, Takuya Nemoto, in Japan.
It is a personal, non-commercial project.
It is not run by a company, a university or a publisher.
The operator runs it as an unpaid volunteer, and is at present the only moderator. It is served only within free services; the operator pays personally for Claude Code, with which it is written.
The operator keeps it as a hobby, as an extension of a personal reading shelf; why it exists and what that means for the records is in the [Disclaimer](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.html).

- ORCID iD: [0009-0000-1406-0547](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547)
- GitHub: [cpsbvbng26-dotcom](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom)

About the operator, the site shows the name, the ORCID iD and the GitHub account above, and nothing more: no photograph, no telephone number and no postal address, which is given on request as "Postal address" below says.

The operator is also the moderator, and is responsible for the site and its records.
The site and its code were built with Claude Code (Anthropic) at the operator's request; see the [Disclaimer](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.html).
The authors bear full responsibility for their works, as the [Terms of Use](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/terms.html) set out.
Submissions by the operator are moderated under the same rules and are marked as the operator's own.
There is no advisory board yet; the call for one is on [Advisory board: a call](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/advisory.html). Advisers will be named here, with an ORCID iD, once they agree.
Introducing Sophaxis: [the page for anyone introducing it](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/press.html), and [the name, logo and badge](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/brand.html).

## Contact

Complaints, legal matters and anything about personal data go by email, not to a public issue: use the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547).
Personal data in an email is used only to answer it, as the [Privacy Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/privacy.html) sets out.

- Questions, suggestions and problems with the site: [an issue](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new).
- Submitting a preprint or a new version: [the submission form](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=submission.yml), or the same form [in Japanese](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=submission-ja.yml).
- An error in a record: [the correction form](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=correction.yml).
- Withdrawing a work, as one of its authors: [the withdrawal form](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=withdrawal.yml).
- Reporting the published version of a listed work, as one of its authors: [the published-version form](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=published.yml).
- Removal for legal reasons: [the removal form](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis/issues/new?template=removal.yml).
- Anything that should not be public: email to the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547).

Issues are public. Do not put personal data in them.
The email address for requests is kept on the ORCID record, not on this site.
The OAI-PMH interface at `/oai` gives a separate address made for harvesters, because the protocol requires one.
Write in English or Japanese.
The email address on the operator's ORCID record, not the one for harvesters, is also the single point of contact under the Digital Services Act of the European Union (Articles 11 and 12), for authorities, the European Commission and people who use Sophaxis.
The operator aims to answer within 7 days.

<!-- text: DSA 11; DSA 12 -->

## Sophaxis elsewhere

- OSF: the project page [Sophaxis: An Independent Overlay Preprint Server](https://osf.io/mq7za/), with the DOI [10.17605/OSF.IO/MQ7ZA](https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/MQ7ZA). The DOI names the project, not a listed work.
- Zenodo: the code and the records, archived with each release. Version 1.0.0 has the DOI [10.5281/zenodo.24033372](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24033372); [10.5281/zenodo.24033371](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24033371) stands for every version. The community <https://zenodo.org/communities/sophaxis> gathers the Zenodo records of works listed on Sophaxis; it is not an affiliation with Zenodo.
- GitHub: the [public repository](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/sophaxis) with the code, the records and the submissions.
- ROAR: Sophaxis passed the editorial review of the Registry of Open Access Repositories at the University of Southampton, and has been listed there since 2026-11-06 (Japan time): [record 27422](https://roar.eprints.org/27422/).
- Open Access Directory: Sophaxis has been listed under Philosophy and under Mathematics on its [Disciplinary repositories](https://oad.simmons.edu/oadwiki/Disciplinary_repositories) page since 2026-11-09 (Japan time). The operator added the entry, and the listing is not a review of Sophaxis.
- X: the official account [@SophaxisX](https://x.com/SophaxisX), with new records and news. The handle ends in X because @Sophaxis was already taken; that account is not Sophaxis.

## Security

A security problem goes by email, not to a public issue, so that it can be fixed before it is known.
Say what you found and how to reproduce it.
Sophaxis offers no reward, and thanks every report.
The site gives the same contact in the standard file [security.txt](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/.well-known/security.txt).

## Accessibility

Sophaxis aims to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA.
Its checks confirm the contrast of every text colour in the light and dark schemes, a link to skip to the content, a visible focus for keyboard users, the language of every page, one main heading per page, and headers for every table.
A barrier can be reported in an issue with the label `accessibility`, or by email.
If a page cannot be used, the operator provides the same information in another form on request, such as plain text by email.
The full statement, with what is checked and what is known not to work, is on [Accessibility](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/accessibility.html).

## Postal address

The operator's postal address is not published.
It is given on request, without delay, as Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information provides.
Ask for it by email.

## Where the site runs

The site is hosted on Vercel and built from the public repository on GitHub.
The code, the records and the issues are kept on GitHub, and the automatic checks run as GitHub Actions there.
Sophaxis is not affiliated with GitHub or Vercel; see the [Disclaimer](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/disclaimer.html).
Repositories and DOI registration agencies can read what Sophaxis takes from them on [a page of its own](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/repositories.html).

# Advisory board: a call

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [諮問委員の募集（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/advisory.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

## Why

Sophaxis has no editorial board and no advisory body; the [transparency self-assessment](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/transparency.html) marks this as not met.
Since 2026-11-10 the operator has invited researchers to form an advisory board.
Until someone agrees and is named on the [Operator and contact](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/contact.html) page, there is no board.

## What an adviser does

- Reads a proposed change to the policies before it is announced, and says what they think, in its public issue or by email.
- Advises on the scope of the fields and on hard cases, when the operator asks.
- Gives no decision on any submission. Moderators are invited separately, as the [Moderation Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/moderation.html) sets out.
- Speaks for themselves only. Advising Sophaxis says nothing about the quality of any listed work, and does not involve the adviser's institution.

The operator decides, and stays responsible for the site and its records.

## Who can join

- A researcher in philosophy, mathematics, logic, the philosophy of mathematics or the philosophy of science.
- Whose public ORCID record lists a journal article, a book chapter or a book with a DOI.
- Who does not live in, or stay in, a place where Sophaxis is not offered, as the [Submission Policy](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/policies/submission.html) lists them.

An adviser is not paid and pays nothing.
An adviser can leave at any time by saying so; their name then leaves the contact page, and the date they left is kept.

## How to join

Write to the operator by email, at the address on the operator's [ORCID record](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-1406-0547), with your ORCID iD and a sentence on why you would like to advise.
The operator decides whom to invite, and answers every message.
Each adviser is named, with an ORCID iD, on the contact page, only after they agree to it.

## Conflicts of interest

An adviser who submits a work goes through the same moderation as anyone else, with no priority.
An adviser does not advise on a case that concerns their own work, or the work of a close collaborator.

Before being named, an adviser declares the following, and the contact page shows the declaration beside the name:

- Any position held now at a repository, publisher, journal, preprint server or index.
- Any payment received in the last three years from one of them.
- Any listed work of their own, or of a close collaborator, on Sophaxis.
- Anything else that a reader might reasonably see as a conflict, or that there is none.

The declaration is updated whenever it changes. An adviser who declares nothing is not named.

Source: https://sophaxis.vercel.app/brand.html

# Name, logo and badge

Last updated: 2026-11-11.

Japanese: [名前・ロゴ・バッジ（日本語訳）](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/brand.ja.html). It is a translation; where the two differ, the English text applies.

## Name

The name is written Sophaxis, in Latin letters, with a capital S, in every language.
In Japanese it is read ソファクシス.
It joins the Greek sophia (σοφία), wisdom, and the Latin axis; the [History and name](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/history.html) page says more.
A record is cited by its Sophaxis id, such as `2026.0001`, and by the DOI of the deposited work.
On 2026-11-11 (Japan time), the operator searched J-PlatPat, the database of the Japan Patent Office, and the WIPO Global Brand Database for the name Sophaxis, and found no trade mark of that name. A search shows only what those databases held that day, and it is not legal advice. The operator has not applied to register the name.

## Logo

The logo is drawn with rectangles and polygons only, so that it looks the same on every device and uses no typeface.

- [favicon.svg](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/favicon.svg): the logo as a vector image.
- [og.png](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/og.png): the logo as a square PNG.

Use the logo unchanged, to refer to Sophaxis or to link to it.
Do not use it in a way that suggests that Sophaxis reviewed, recommends or is connected with something it is not.

## Colours

| Use | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `#f7f5f0` | `#14171f` |
| Text | `#1d2330` | `#e6e2d8` |
| Accent | `#2f4a7a` | `#9fb6e0` |

## Badge for a listed work

An author of a listed work can show that it is listed, with the badge [badge.svg](https://sophaxis.vercel.app/badge.svg).
Each record page gives the badge with a link to that record, ready to paste.

- Use it only for a work that Sophaxis lists, and link it to the record page.
- Remove it if the work is withdrawn or its record is removed.
- The badge says that the work passed moderation. It does not say that the work was peer-reviewed, and it says nothing of its quality.

## Text of the site

The text of the site is shared under CC BY 4.0 and its code under MIT, as every page says.
